cards.a: High Calcium-Phosphate product and Warfarin use in ESRD patients.

cards.q: Distinction between "Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica" and "Adynamic Bone Disease"?
cards.a: Osteitis is high bone turnover (high PTH); Adynamic is low bone turnover (over-suppressed PTH). Part 24: Practical Management Nuances

cards.q: Definition of "Resistance" to Loop Diuretics?
cards.a: Hypertrophy of the distal tubule allows for compensatory $NaCl$ reabsorption.

cards.q: Strategy to overcome Loop Diuretic resistance?
cards.a: "Sequential Nephron Blockade" by adding a Thiazide (e.g., Metolazone).

cards.q: Indication for Sodium Bicarbonate in CKD patients?
cards.a: Serum $HCO_3 < 22$ mEq/L (to slow progression of CKD and bone loss).

cards.q: When to initiate Dialysis in CKD (non-urgent)?
cards.a: Usually when GFR is $< 10$ mL/min or when uremic symptoms (nausea, pericarditis, encephalopathy) appear.

cards.q: Preferred vascular access for long-term Hemodialysis?
cards.a: Arteriovenous (AV) Fistula (lowest infection and thrombosis rates).

cards.q: How long does an AV Fistula typically need to "mature" before use?
cards.a: 6 to 8 weeks.

cards.q: Most common cause of EPO-resistant anemia in CKD?
cards.a: Iron deficiency. Part 25: Rapid-Fire Differentials

cards.q: Patient with Nephrotic syndrome + Macroglossia + Heart Failure?
cards.a: Renal Amyloidosis.

cards.q: Apple-green birefringence under polarized light (Congo Red stain)?
cards.a: Amyloidosis.

cards.q: Hematuria + Flank Pain + Palpable Mass?
cards.a: Renal Cell Carcinoma triad (though rarely all three appear together).

cards.q: Most common histologic type of Renal Cell Carcinoma?
cards.a: Clear Cell Carcinoma.

cards.q: Paraneoplastic syndrome associated with Renal Cell Carcinoma?
cards.a: Erythrocytosis (due to EPO production).

cards.q: Patient with "Muddy Brown Casts" + high FeNa after a long surgery?
cards.a: Ischemic Acute Tubular Necrosis (ATN).

cards.q: Sudden AKI + "Humps" on EM + Low C3?
cards.a: Post-streptococcal Glomerulonephritis.

cards.q: Definition of Laboratory Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS)?
cards.a: Hyperuricemia, hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, and hypocalcemia.

cards.q: Mechanism of AKI in Tumor Lysis Syndrome?
cards.a: Intratubular precipitation of uric acid and calcium phosphate crystals.

cards.q: Preferred agent to prevent TLS in high-risk patients?
cards.a: Allopurinol (blocks xanthine oxidase).

cards.q: Agent used to treat acute, existing hyperuricemia in TLS?
cards.a: Rasburicase (recombinant urate oxidase that converts uric acid to allantoin).

cards.q: Common cause of "Bland" urine sediment but rising SCr in a Multiple Myeloma patient?
cards.a: Myeloma Kidney (Light Chain Cast Nephropathy).

cards.q: Nephrotic syndrome classic to Hodgkin Lymphoma?
cards.a: Minimal Change Disease. Part 27: Diuretic Resistance & Advanced Pharma

cards.q: The "Braking Phenomenon" in diuretic therapy?
cards.a: The kidney's compensatory increase in sodium reabsorption in response to chronic loop diuretic use.

cards.q: Mechanism of Furosemide in treating pulmonary edema (besides diuresis)?
cards.a: Rapid venous dilation (increasing venous capacitance) before the onset of diuresis.

cards.q: Electrolyte abnormality caused by Loop Diuretics that can lead to metabolic alkalosis?
cards.a: Contraction Alkalosis (loss of chloride-rich, bicarbonate-poor fluid).

cards.q: Why are Thiazides ineffective when GFR is $< 30$ mL/min?
cards.a: They cannot reach their site of action in the distal tubule (Metolazone is a notable exception).

cards.q: Mechanism of Acetazolamide-induced Metabolic Acidosis?
cards.a: Inhibition of proximal tubule $HCO_3^-$ reabsorption leads to increased bicarbonate excretion. Part 28: Geriatric & Critical Care Nephrology

cards.q: Why is Serum Creatinine an unreliable marker of GFR in the elderly?
cards.a: Decreased muscle mass leads to lower creatinine production, masking significant renal impairment.

cards.q: Most common cause of Hyponatremia in the elderly on new medication?
cards.a: Thiazide-induced hyponatremia.

cards.q: Distinguishing feature between Hyponatremia caused by SIADH vs. Salt-Wasting?
cards.a: Salt-Wasting involves volume depletion (hypovolemia); SIADH is euvolemic.

cards.q: First-line treatment for "Hepatorenal Syndrome Type 1"?
cards.a: Albumin and Vasoconstrictors (e.g., Terlipressin or Norepinephrine).

cards.q: Classic renal biopsy finding in "Myoglobinuric AKI"?
cards.a: Pigmented granular casts and tubular necrosis. Part 29: Glomerular Nuances & Rare GN

cards.q: Serum Complement level (C3/C4) in IgA Nephropathy?
cards.a: Characteristically Normal.

cards.q: Most common extra-renal finding in IgA Vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein)?
cards.a: Palpable purpura on the lower extremities and buttocks.

cards.q: Renal syndrome associated with "Anti-Phospholipase A2 Receptor" (PLA2R) antibodies?
cards.a: Primary Membranous Nephropathy.

cards.q: Pathogenesis of Alport Syndrome?
cards.a: Mutation in the alpha-3, 4, or 5 chains of Type IV Collagen.

cards.q: EM finding in Alport Syndrome?
cards.a: Irregular thinning and thickening of the GBM ("Basket-weave" appearance).

cards.q: Classic feature of Thin Basement Membrane Disease?
cards.a: Persistent, benign microscopic hematuria with a normal family history of renal function. Part 30: Electrolyte "Double-Checks"

cards.q: Why does Hypermagnesemia cause Hypocalcemia?
cards.a: It suppresses Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) secretion.

cards.q: Most common cause of Hypoxemia during a Hemodialysis session?
cards.a: Acetate in the dialysate or complement activation on the dialysis membrane leading to pulmonary sequestration of WBCs.

cards.q: Preferred treatment for Hyperkalemia in a patient with Metabolic Acidosis?
cards.a: Sodium Bicarbonate (shifts $K^+$ into cells while treating the underlying pH).

cards.q: ECG finding classic for Hypocalcemia?
cards.a: Prolonged QT interval (predisposes to arrhythmias).

cards.q: Corrected Sodium formula for Hyperglycemia (the "1.6" rule)?
cards.a: $Corrected\ Na = Measured\ Na + 0.016 \times (Glucose - 100)$. Part 31: Transplant Immunology & Rejection

cards.q: Timeframe for "Chronic Rejection" of a renal transplant?
cards.a: Months to years after transplant.

cards.q: Primary pathology in Chronic Transplant Rejection?
cards.a: Vascular fibrosis and "Graft Arteriopathy" (intimal thickening).

cards.q: Role of BK Virus in transplant nephropathy?
cards.a: Reactivation of the polyomavirus leads to tubulointerstitial inflammation and graft loss.

cards.q: Most common cause of Post-transplant Erythrocytosis?
cards.a: Overproduction of EPO by the native kidneys or the graft (treated with ACE inhibitors). Part 32: Rapid-Fire Differentials (Summary Cards)

cards.q: Hematuria + Hemoptysis + Anti-GBM (+)?
cards.a: Goodpasture Syndrome.

cards.q: Hematuria + Hemoptysis + c-ANCA (+)?
cards.a: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (Wegener’s).

cards.q: Hematuria + Asthma + p-ANCA (+)?
cards.a: Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (Churg-Strauss).

cards.q: Hematuria + Deafness + Family History (+)?
cards.a: Alport Syndrome.

cards.q: Hematuria + Recent Pharyngitis (1-3 days prior)?
cards.a: IgA Nephropathy.

cards.q: Hematuria + Recent Pharyngitis (2 weeks prior) + Low C3?
cards.a: Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephritis (PSGN).

cards.q: Hematuria + HIV + Heroin Use + Nephrotic range proteinuria?
cards.a: Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis (FSGS).

cards.q: Definition of "Renal Reserve"?
cards.a: The ability of the kidney to increase GFR in response to a protein load or amino acid infusion.

cards.q: Why does Urea reabsorption increase in states of dehydration?
cards.a: ADH (Vasopressin) increases the permeability of the medullary collecting duct to urea to maintain the osmotic gradient.

cards.q: Formula for "Free Water Clearance" ($C_{H2O}$)?
cards.a: $C_{H2O} = V - \frac{U_{osm} \times V}{P_{osm}}$.

cards.q: Significance of a negative Free Water Clearance?
cards.a: The kidney is conserving water (producing concentrated urine), typical in states of ADH excess.

cards.q: What does "Urine Osmolar Gap" measure?
cards.a: It estimates ammonium ($NH_4^+$) excretion in Normal Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis.

cards.q: Calculation for Urine Osmolar Gap?
cards.a: $U_{osm} (measured) - [2(Na + K) + \frac{Urea}{2.8} + \frac{Glucose}{18}]$. Part 34: Nephrolithiasis & Crystal Arthropathy

cards.q: Primary inhibitor of calcium stone formation found in normal urine?
cards.a: Citrate (it chelates calcium in the urine).

cards.q: Most common cause of Hypercalciuria with normal serum calcium?
cards.a: Idiopathic Hypercalciuria.

cards.q: Why does Crohn’s Disease increase the risk of Calcium Oxalate stones?
cards.a: Fat malabsorption binds calcium in the gut, leaving oxalate free to be absorbed (Enteric Hyperoxaluria).

cards.q: Classic urine crystal finding in Ethylene Glycol ingestion?
cards.a: Monohydrate calcium oxalate (needle/dumbbell shaped) or dihydrate (envelope shaped).

cards.q: Mechanism of "Indinavir Stones"?
cards.a: Precipitation of the protease inhibitor medication itself; these stones are radiolucent on CT. Part 35: Vascular & Ischemic Renal Disease

cards.q: Definition of "Flash Pulmonary Edema" in Nephrology?
cards.a: Sudden, severe pulmonary edema often associated with bilateral renal artery stenosis.

cards.q: Preferred screening test for Renal Artery Stenosis in patients with CKD?
cards.a: Doppler Ultrasound or MR Angiography (avoiding CT with contrast).

cards.q: Most common cause of Renal Artery Stenosis in elderly males?
cards.a: Atherosclerosis.

cards.q: Renal biopsy finding in Malignant Hypertension?
cards.a: Hyperplastic arteriolitis ("onion-skinning") and fibrinoid necrosis.

cards.q: Typical presentation of Renal Artery Embolism?
cards.a: Acute flank pain, nausea, and high LDH with a normal urine sediment. Part 36: Pediatric & Congenital Anomalies

cards.q: Most common cause of bladder outlet obstruction in newborn males?
cards.a: Posterior Urethral Valves.

cards.q: Diagnostic test of choice for Posterior Urethral Valves?
cards.a: Voiding Cystourethrogram (VCUG).

cards.q: Mnemonic for Potter Sequence (resulting from oligohydramnios)?
cards.a: Pulmonary hypoplasia, Oligohydramnios, Twisted face, Twisted skin, Extremity defects, Renal failure.

cards.q: Most common cause of a palpable abdominal mass in a newborn?
cards.a: Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney (MCDK).

cards.q: Genetic defect in Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease (ARPKD)?
cards.a: Mutation in the PKHD1 gene (fibrocystin).

cards.q: Systemic finding always present in ARPKD?
cards.a: Congenital Hepatic Fibrosis. Part 37: Advanced Fluid Management

cards.q: Definition of "Isotonic saline" ($0.9\% NaCl$) osmolality?
cards.a: 308 mOsm/L.

cards.q: Why can $0.9\%$ Saline cause a Normal Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis?
cards.a: The high chloride load ($154$ mEq/L) drives bicarbonate out of the plasma (Hyperchloremic Acidosis).

cards.q: Preferred fluid for resuscitation in Hypernatremic Dehydration?
cards.a: Initial Isotonic Saline (to restore BP), followed by $5\%$ Dextrose ($D5W$) or $0.45\%$ Saline.

cards.q: Formula for "Free Water Deficit" in Hypernatremia?
cards.a: $0.6 \times Weight \times (\frac{Current\ Na}{140} - 1)$. Part 38: Kidney in Systemic Disease (The "Connectors")

cards.q: Most common renal lesion in patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis?
cards.a: AA Amyloidosis (secondary to chronic inflammation).

cards.q: Effect of NSAIDs on Renal Blood Flow in a "low-effective-circulating-volume" state?
cards.a: They block vasodilatory prostaglandins, leading to acute prerenal failure.

cards.q: Distinguishing feature of Lithium-induced Nephrogenic DI vs. others?
cards.a: It can persist even after the drug is discontinued due to permanent collecting duct damage.

cards.q: Classic renal finding in Sarcoidosis?
cards.a: Hypercalciuria and Hypercalcemia (due to extra-renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase in granulomas).

cards.q: Renal biopsy finding in Sjogren’s Syndrome?
cards.a: Chronic Interstitial Nephritis, often presenting as Type 1 RTA. Part 39: End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) Management

cards.q: Leading cause of death in the first year of starting Dialysis?
cards.a: Infection (specifically catheter-related sepsis).

cards.q: Target "Urea Reduction Ratio" (URR) for adequate dialysis?
cards.a: Greater than $65\%$.

cards.q: Definition of "Disequilibrium Syndrome" during dialysis?
cards.a: Cerebral edema caused by the rapid removal of urea from the blood while it remains high in the brain.

cards.q: Primary treatment for Uremic Pericarditis?
cards.a: Immediate intensification of Hemodialysis.

cards.q: Why is Heparin used during Hemodialysis?
cards.a: To prevent clotting of the blood within the extracorporeal circuit/dialyzer. Part 40: Acid-Base "Must-Knows"

cards.q: Most common cause of Respiratory Alkalosis in a clinical setting?
cards.a: Hyperventilation (Anxiety, Pain, or early Sepsis).

cards.q: Expected compensation for Acute Respiratory Acidosis?
cards.a: Bicarbonate increases by $1$ mEq/L for every $10$ mmHg increase in $PCO_2$.

cards.q: Expected compensation for Chronic Respiratory Acidosis?
cards.a: Bicarbonate increases by $3.5$ to $4$ mEq/L for every $10$ mmHg increase in $PCO_2$.

cards.q: Definition of "Metabolic Alkalosis, Saline-Resistant"?
cards.a: Urinary Chloride $> 20$ mEq/L; usually due to mineralocorticoid excess.

cards.q: Definition of "Metabolic Alkalosis, Saline-Responsive"?
Diagnostic criteria for DM based on Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG)?
cards.a: $\ge 126$ mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L).

cards.q: Diagnostic criteria for DM based on HbA1c?
Diagnostic criteria for DM based on 2-hour Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT)?
cards.a: $\ge 200$ mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L).

cards.q: Definition of "Prediabetes" by HbA1c range?
Primary pathology in Type 1 DM?
cards.a: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells leading to absolute insulin deficiency.

cards.q: Most common autoantibody checked in Type 1 DM?
cards.a: Glutamic Acid Decarboxylase (GAD-65) antibodies.

cards.q: Primary pathology in Type 2 DM?
cards.a: Insulin resistance combined with relative insulin deficiency.

cards.q: First-line pharmacological treatment for Type 2 DM?
cards.a: Metformin.

cards.q: Major contraindication for Metformin use?
cards.a: Estimated GFR < 30 mL/min (risk of lactic acidosis).

cards.q: Mechanism of action of Sulfonylureas (e.g., Glipizide)?
cards.a: Closes ATP-sensitive K+ channels in beta cells to stimulate insulin release.

cards.q: Primary side effect of Sulfonylureas?
cards.a: Hypoglycemia and weight gain.

cards.q: Mechanism of SGLT-2 inhibitors (e.g., Empagliflozin)?
cards.a: Inhibits glucose reabsorption in the proximal convoluted tubule, causing glucosuria.

cards.q: Specific benefit of SGLT-2 inhibitors in comorbid patients?
cards.a: Reduction in heart failure hospitalizations and progression of CKD.

cards.q: Common side effect of SGLT-2 inhibitors?
cards.a: Euglycemic DKA and Genitourinary yeast infections.

cards.q: Mechanism of GLP-1 agonists (e.g., Liraglutide, Semaglutide)?
cards.a: Increases glucose-dependent insulin secretion, slows gastric emptying, increases satiety.

cards.q: GLP-1 agonists are contraindicated in patients with a history of?
cards.a: Medullary Thyroid Cancer or MEN 2 (due to C-cell hyperplasia risk).

cards.q: Clinical triad of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)?
cards.a: Hyperglycemia, Ketosis (Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis), and Dehydration.

cards.q: Best initial step in management of DKA?
cards.a: Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation (Normal Saline).

cards.q: When should Potassium be added to IV fluids in DKA management?
cards.a: When serum K+ is < 5.2 mEq/L (insulin will shift K+ intracellularly).

cards.q: Distinctive feature of Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS) compared to DKA?
cards.a: Extreme hyperglycemia (> 600 mg/dL), high serum osmolality, and absence of significant ketoacidosis.

cards.q: Screening frequency for diabetic retinopathy and nephropathy?
cards.a: Annually (starting at diagnosis for T2DM; 5 years after diagnosis for T1DM).

cards.q: First sign of diabetic nephropathy on labs?
cards.a: Moderately increased albuminuria (Microalbuminuria, 30–300 mg/day). Section 2: Thyroid Disorders

cards.q: Most common cause of Hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions?
cards.a: Hashimoto Thyroiditis (Chronic Autoimmune Thyroiditis).

cards.q: Best initial screening test for thyroid function?
cards.a: Serum TSH.

cards.q: Serum TSH and Free T4 levels in Subclinical Hypothyroidism?
cards.a: Elevated TSH with normal Free T4.

cards.q: Serum TSH and Free T4 levels in Secondary (Central) Hypothyroidism?
cards.a: Low or inappropriately normal TSH with low Free T4.

cards.q: Most common cause of Hyperthyroidism?
cards.a: Graves Disease.

cards.q: Pathognomonic physical exam findings in Graves Disease?
cards.a: Exophthalmos (proptosis) and Pretibial Myxedema.

cards.q: Antibody associated with Graves Disease?
cards.a: Thyroid Stimulating Immunoglobulin (TSI) or TSH-receptor antibodies.

cards.q: Radioactive Iodine Uptake (RAIU) pattern in Graves Disease?
cards.a: Diffuse, increased uptake.

cards.q: RAIU pattern in Toxic Multinodular Goiter?
cards.a: Patchy, focal areas of increased uptake ("Hot" nodules).

cards.q: RAIU pattern in Subacute (de Quervain) Thyroiditis?
cards.a: Decreased or low uptake (due to release of preformed hormone/inflammation).

cards.q: Clinical presentation of de Quervain Thyroiditis?
cards.a: Painful/tender thyroid gland, often following a viral URI.

cards.q: Management of de Quervain Thyroiditis?
cards.a: NSAIDs and Beta-blockers (self-limiting).

cards.q: Serious side effect of Thionamides (PTU/Methimazole)?
cards.a: Agranulocytosis.

cards.q: Preferred Thionamide in the first trimester of pregnancy?
cards.a: Propylthiouracil (PTU).

cards.q: Preferred Thionamide for most non-pregnant patients and 2nd/3rd trimester?
cards.a: Methimazole (due to lower hepatotoxicity).

cards.q: Characteristic EKG finding in Myxedema Coma?
cards.a: Bradycardia and low voltage complexes.

cards.q: Treatment for Thyroid Storm?
cards.a: Propranolol, PTU, IV Iodine (1 hour after PTU), and Glucocorticoids.

cards.q: Most common type of Thyroid Cancer?
cards.a: Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.

cards.q: Histological hallmarks of Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma?
cards.a: Orphan Annie eye nuclei and Psammoma bodies.

cards.q: Thyroid cancer associated with MEN 2A and 2B?
cards.a: Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma (derived from C-cells; produces Calcitonin).

cards.q: Management of a thyroid nodule with low TSH?
cards.a: Perform Thyroid Scintigraphy (RAIU scan).

cards.q: Management of a thyroid nodule > 1cm with normal/high TSH?
cards.a: Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA). Section 3: Adrenal Gland Disorders

cards.q: Most common cause of Primary Adrenal Insufficiency (Addison's) worldwide?
cards.a: Tuberculosis (Autoimmune in developed countries).

cards.q: Electrolyte abnormalities in Primary Adrenal Insufficiency?
cards.a: Hyponatremia, Hyperkalemia, and Hyperchloremic Metabolic Acidosis.

cards.q: Why does skin hyperpigmentation occur in Addison's Disease?
cards.a: High ACTH levels lead to increased Melanocyte-Stimulating Hormone (MSH) production.

cards.q: Best initial test for suspected Adrenal Insufficiency?
cards.a: 8 AM Serum Cortisol and ACTH.

cards.q: Definitive diagnostic test for Adrenal Insufficiency?
cards.a: Cosyntropin (ACTH) Stimulation Test.

cards.q: Management of Acute Adrenal Crisis?
cards.a: High-dose IV Hydrocortisone and aggressive IV fluids.

cards.q: Difference between Cushing Syndrome and Cushing Disease?
cards.a: Syndrome is any cause of hypercortisolism; Disease is specifically a pituitary ACTH-secreting adenoma.

cards.q: Most common overall cause of Cushing Syndrome?
cards.a: Exogenous glucocorticoid administration.

cards.q: First-line screening tests for Cushing Syndrome (choose one)?
cards.a: 24-hour urinary free cortisol, late-night salivary cortisol, or Low-dose Dexamethasone Suppression Test.

cards.q: Results of High-dose Dexamethasone Suppression Test in Cushing Disease?
cards.a: Cortisol levels suppress by > 50%.

cards.q: Results of High-dose Dexamethasone Suppression Test in Ectopic ACTH (e.g., Small Cell Lung Cancer)?
cards.a: No suppression of cortisol.

cards.q: Classic triad of Pheochromocytoma?
cards.a: Episodic headache, diaphoresis, and tachycardia (with hypertension).

cards.q: Best initial screening test for Pheochromocytoma?
cards.a: Plasma or 24-hour urinary metanephrines.

cards.q: Pre-operative management order for Pheochromocytoma?
cards.a: Alpha-blockade (Phenoxybenzamine) first, then Beta-blockade.

cards.q: Primary Hyperaldosteronism (Conn Syndrome) triad?
cards.a: Hypertension, Hypokalemia, and Metabolic Alkalosis.

cards.q: Screening test for Primary Hyperaldosteronism?
cards.a: Plasma Aldosterone to Plasma Renin Activity (PAC/PRA) ratio > 20.

cards.q: Most common cause of Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH)?
cards.a: 21-hydroxylase deficiency.

cards.q: Lab finding in 21-hydroxylase deficiency?
cards.a: Elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone. Section 4: Pituitary and Hypothalamus

cards.q: Most common functional (secretory) pituitary adenoma?
cards.a: Prolactinoma.

cards.q: Clinical presentation of Prolactinoma in women?
cards.a: Galactorrhea, amenorrhea, and infertility.

cards.q: First-line treatment for Prolactinomas?
cards.a: Dopamine agonists (Cabergoline or Bromocriptine).

cards.q: Gold standard test for diagnosing Acromegaly?
cards.a: Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (failure to suppress Growth Hormone).

cards.q: Screening test for Acromegaly?
cards.a: Serum Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1).

cards.q: Clinical features of Acromegaly?
cards.a: Enlarged hands/feet, frontal bossing, macroglossia, and new-onset Sleep Apnea or DM.

cards.q: Definition of Diabetes Insipidus (DI)?
cards.a: Passage of large volumes (> 3L/day) of dilute urine (Osmolality < 300).

cards.q: Central vs. Nephrogenic DI response to Desmopressin (DDAVP)?
cards.a: Central DI shows > 50% increase in urine osmolality; Nephrogenic DI shows little to no response.

cards.q: Common medication cause of Nephrogenic DI?
cards.a: Lithium.

cards.q: Electrolyte hallmark of SIADH?
cards.a: Euvolemic Hyponatremia.

cards.q: Management of mild SIADH?
cards.a: Fluid restriction.

cards.q: Dangerous complication of correcting hyponatremia too rapidly?
cards.a: Osmotic Demyelination Syndrome (Central Pontine Myelinolysis).

cards.q: Safe rate of sodium correction in chronic hyponatremia?
cards.a: < 8-10 mEq/L in 24 hours.

cards.q: Definition of Sheehan Syndrome?
cards.a: Ischemic necrosis of the pituitary gland following severe postpartum hemorrhage.

cards.q: Early sign of Sheehan Syndrome?
cards.a: Failure to lactate (loss of prolactin). Section 5: Calcium and Bone Metabolism

cards.q: Most common cause of Primary Hyperparathyroidism?
cards.a: Solitary Parathyroid Adenoma.

cards.q: Lab findings in Primary Hyperparathyroidism?
cards.a: Elevated Calcium, Low Phosphorus, Elevated PTH, Elevated Vitamin D.

cards.q: Radiographic finding classic for Hyperparathyroidism?
cards.a: Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica (salt-and-pepper skull, subperiosteal bone resorption).

cards.q: Primary cause of Secondary Hyperparathyroidism?
cards.a: Chronic Kidney Disease (low Vitamin D/High Phos leading to high PTH).

cards.q: Definition of Tertiary Hyperparathyroidism?
cards.a: Autonomous PTH secretion following long-standing secondary hyperparathyroidism.

cards.q: Chvostek and Trousseau signs indicate?
cards.a: Hypocalcemia.

cards.q: EKG finding in Hypocalcemia?
cards.a: Prolonged QT interval.

cards.q: EKG finding in Hypercalcemia?
cards.a: Shortened QT interval.

cards.q: First-line treatment for symptomatic or severe Hypercalcemia (>14)?
cards.a: Aggressive IV hydration (Normal Saline).

cards.q: T-score range for Osteopenia?
T-score for Osteoporosis?
First-line pharmacological treatment for Osteoporosis?
cards.a: Bisphosphonates (e.g., Alendronate). Section 6: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN)

cards.q: Components of MEN 1 (3 Ps)?
cards.a: Pituitary adenoma, Parathyroid hyperplasia, Pancreatic tumors (Zollinger-Ellison).

cards.q: Components of MEN 2A (1 M, 2 Ps)?
cards.a: Medullary thyroid cancer, Pheochromocytoma, Parathyroid hyperplasia.

cards.q: Components of MEN 2B (2 Ms, 1 P)?
cards.a: Medullary thyroid cancer, Marfanoid habitus/Mucosal neuromas, Pheochromocytoma.

cards.q: Gene mutation associated with MEN 2A and 2B?
cards.a: RET proto-oncogene. Section 7: Reproductive Endocrinology (Internal Medicine context)

cards.q: Most common cause of hirsutism and infertility in women?
cards.a: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS).

cards.q: Lab ratio suggestive of PCOS?
cards.a: LH:FSH ratio > 2:1 (though not diagnostic).

cards.q: Primary risk associated with untreated PCOS?
cards.a: Endometrial Hyperplasia/Cancer (due to unopposed estrogen).

cards.q: Definition of Klinefelter Syndrome karyotype?
cards.a: 47, XXY.

cards.q: Physical findings in Klinefelter Syndrome?
cards.a: Small firm testes, gynecomastia, tall stature, and primary hypogonadism.

cards.q: Definition of Kallmann Syndrome?
cards.a: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia (failed migration of GnRH neurons). Section 8: Miscellaneous High-Yield

cards.q: Serum marker for monitoring Medullary Thyroid Cancer recurrence?
cards.a: Calcitonin.

cards.q: Serum marker for monitoring Papillary/Follicular Thyroid Cancer recurrence?
cards.a: Thyroglobulin.

cards.q: Diagnosis of VIPoma (WDHA Syndrome)?
cards.a: Watery Diarrhea, Hypokalemia, Achlorhydria.

cards.q: Diagnosis of Glucagonoma?
cards.a: Necrolytic Migratory Erythema, Weight loss, and Diabetes.

cards.q: Primary hormone deficiency in Polyglandular Autoimmune Syndrome Type 1?
cards.a: Hypoparathyroidism, Adrenal Insufficiency, and Mucocutaneous Candidiasis.

cards.q: "Rule of 10s" for Pheochromocytoma?
cards.a: 10% bilateral, 10% malignant, 10% extra-adrenal, 10% familial.

cards.q: Effect of Estrogen (Pregnancy/OCPs) on thyroid lab values?
cards.a: Increases Thyroid Binding Globulin (TBG), increasing Total T4, but Free T4 remains normal.

cards.q: Most common cause of death in patients with Acromegaly?
cards.a: Heart Failure (dilated cardiomyopathy).

cards.q: Medical treatment to reduce GH in Acromegaly?
cards.a: Octreotide or Lanreotide (Somatostatin analogs).

cards.q: Definition of Nelson Syndrome?
cards.a: Rapid enlargement of an ACTH-secreting pituitary adenoma after bilateral adrenalectomy. Section 9: Advanced Diabetes Management & Complications

cards.q: What is the "Somogyi Effect"?
cards.a: Rebound hyperglycemia in the morning caused by a response to hypoglycemia during the night.

cards.q: What is the "Dawn Phenomenon"?
cards.a: Morning hyperglycemia due to the natural early-morning surge of Growth Hormone and Cortisol.

cards.q: Preferred screening test for Diabetic Gastroparesis?
cards.a: Gastric emptying study (scintigraphy) with a solid meal.

cards.q: First-line medical treatment for Diabetic Gastroparesis?
cards.a: Metoclopramide or Erythromycin.

cards.q: Management of Diabetic Neuropathy pain?
cards.a: Gabapentin, Pregabalin, or Duloxetine.

cards.q: Most common cause of death in patients with Diabetes Mellitus?
cards.a: Cardiovascular disease (Myocardial Infarction).

cards.q: Diagnostic criteria for Metabolic Syndrome?
cards.a: 3 of 5: Large waist, High TG, Low HDL, HTN, High fasting glucose.

cards.q: Mechanism of Thiazolidinediones (e.g., Pioglitazone)?
cards.a: Activates PPAR-gamma to increase peripheral insulin sensitivity.

cards.q: Major side effects of Pioglitazone?
cards.a: Weight gain, edema, and worsening of Heart Failure.

cards.q: Mechanism of Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors (e.g., Acarbose)?
cards.a: Inhibits intestinal enzymes to delay carbohydrate absorption. Section 10: Specific Thyroid Scenarios

cards.q: Management of Amiodarone-induced Thyrotoxicosis Type 1 (Jod-Basedow)?
cards.a: Thionamides (Methimazole/PTU).

cards.q: Management of Amiodarone-induced Thyrotoxicosis Type 2 (Destructive)?
cards.a: Glucocorticoids.

cards.q: Thyroid finding in Riedel Thyroiditis?
cards.a: "Rock-hard," fixed, painless goiter (fibrosis may extend to adjacent structures).

cards.q: Definition of "Euthyroid Sick Syndrome"?
cards.a: Low T3, normal/low T4, and normal/low TSH in the setting of severe non-thyroidal illness.

cards.q: Most common cause of Euthyroid Sick Syndrome?
cards.a: Critical illness or starvation (decreased peripheral conversion of T4 to T3).

cards.q: Management of Euthyroid Sick Syndrome?
cards.a: Observation and treatment of the underlying illness (do not give levothyroxine).

cards.q: Risk of untreated Subclinical Hyperthyroidism in the elderly?
cards.a: Atrial Fibrillation and Osteoporosis.

cards.q: Thyroid cancer that spreads hematogenously?
cards.a: Follicular Thyroid Carcinoma.

cards.q: Why can't FNA distinguish Follicular Adenoma from Follicular Carcinoma?
cards.a: Carcinoma requires visual evidence of capsular or vascular invasion (not seen on cytology). Section 11: Adrenal Nuances & Surgery

cards.q: Most common cause of Secondary Adrenal Insufficiency?
cards.a: Chronic glucocorticoid therapy followed by abrupt withdrawal.

cards.q: Differentiator between Primary and Secondary Adrenal Insufficiency on labs?
cards.a: Secondary has normal Mineralocorticoid (Aldosterone) levels and no hyperpigmentation.

cards.q: Management of an incidentally discovered adrenal mass (Incidentaloma)?
cards.a: Screen for function (24hr catecholamines, cortisol, and renin/aldosterone).

cards.q: When is surgery indicated for an adrenal incidentaloma?
cards.a: If it is functional (hormone-secreting) or > 4cm in size.

cards.q: Management of Primary Hyperaldosteronism due to bilateral adrenal hyperplasia?
cards.a: Aldosterone antagonists (Spironolactone or Eplerenone).

cards.q: Mechanism of Metyrapone?
cards.a: Inhibits 11-beta-hydroxylase, blocking cortisol synthesis (used in Cushing's testing).

cards.q: Electrolyte finding in Waterhouse-Friderichsen Syndrome?
cards.a: Acute adrenal insufficiency (low Na+, high K+) due to adrenal hemorrhage. Section 12: Hypothalamic & Pituitary Details

cards.q: Triad of McCune-Albright Syndrome?
cards.a: Precocious puberty, Café-au-lait spots (irregular borders), and Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia.

cards.q: Most common cause of Hyperprolactinemia besides Prolactinoma?
cards.a: Medications (especially Antipsychotics/Dopamine antagonists).

cards.q: Mechanism of Pituitary Apoplexy?
cards.a: Sudden hemorrhage or infarction of a pituitary adenoma.

cards.q: First step in suspected Pituitary Apoplexy with visual loss?
cards.a: Urgent surgical decompression and high-dose glucocorticoids.

cards.q: Difference between Psychogenic Polydipsia and DI?
cards.a: In Psychogenic Polydipsia, serum sodium is typically low (dilutional).

cards.q: Lab finding in Empty Sella Syndrome?
cards.a: Often incidental and asymptomatic; pituitary function is usually normal.

cards.q: Most common tumor of the pituitary region in children?
cards.a: Craniopharyngioma.

cards.q: Imaging characteristic of Craniopharyngioma?
cards.a: Suprasellar mass with calcifications on CT. Section 13: Lipid Metabolism (Harrison's Highlights)

cards.q: First-line therapy for isolated Hypertriglyceridemia (> 500 mg/dL)?
cards.a: Fibrates (to prevent Pancreatitis).

cards.q: Mechanism of Statins?
cards.a: HMG-CoA Reductase inhibitors (upregulate LDL receptors).

cards.q: Most common side effect of Statins?
cards.a: Myalgia and (rarely) Rhabdomyolysis.

cards.q: Mechanism of Ezetimibe?
cards.a: Inhibits cholesterol absorption at the brush border of the small intestine.

cards.q: Primary side effect of Niacin?
cards.a: Skin flushing (mediated by prostaglandins; treat with Aspirin).

cards.q: Type I Dyslipidemia (Hyperchylomicronemia) deficiency?
cards.a: Lipoprotein Lipase (LPL) or ApoC-II deficiency.

cards.q: Physical finding in Type II Hypercholesterolemia?
cards.a: Tendon Xanthomas (Achilles) and Xanthelasma.

cards.q: Physical finding in Hypertriglyceridemia?
cards.a: Eruptive Xanthomas (yellow papules on back/buttocks). Section 14: Bone & Mineral (Williams Textbook Focus)

cards.q: Definitive treatment for Vitamin D deficiency (Osteomalacia)?
cards.a: Ergocalciferol or Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D2 or D3) supplementation.

cards.q: Lab values in Vitamin D deficiency?
cards.a: Low Ca, Low Phosphorus, High PTH.

cards.q: Hallmark of Paget’s Disease of Bone on labs?
cards.a: Isolated, severely elevated Alkaline Phosphatase with normal Ca/Phos/PTH.

cards.q: First-line treatment for Paget’s Disease of Bone?
cards.a: Bisphosphonates (to inhibit osteoclast activity).

cards.q: Management of Hungry Bone Syndrome (post-parathyroidectomy)?
cards.a: Aggressive Calcium and Vitamin D supplementation.

cards.q: Cause of Pseudohypoparathyroidism?
cards.a: End-organ resistance to PTH (Albright Hereditary Osteodystrophy).

cards.q: Lab profile of Pseudohypoparathyroidism?
cards.a: Low Calcium, High Phosphorus, High PTH. Section 15: Metabolic Emergency & "Must-Knows"

cards.q: Best fluid choice for a patient in Hypercalcemic Crisis?
cards.a: 0.9% Normal Saline (aggressive rate).

cards.q: Why is Loop Diuretic (Furosemide) use restricted in Hypercalcemia?
cards.a: Only used after volume repletion to prevent fluid overload.

cards.q: Standard medical management for Symptomatic Hypocalcemia?
cards.a: IV Calcium Gluconate.

cards.q: Most common cause of hypercalcemia in the outpatient setting?
cards.a: Primary Hyperparathyroidism.

cards.q: Most common cause of hypercalcemia in the inpatient setting?
cards.a: Malignancy (PTHrP or bone metastases).

cards.q: How to calculate Corrected Calcium?
cards.a: Corrected Ca = [Measured Ca] + 0.8 * (4 - Albumin).

cards.q: Immediate treatment for severe Hyperkalemia with EKG changes?
cards.a: IV Calcium Gluconate (to stabilize the cardiac membrane).

cards.q: Hormonal cause of secondary Hypertension in a young patient with abdominal bruit?
cards.a: Renal Artery Stenosis (Secondary Hyperaldosteronism).

cards.q: Characteristic of Glucagonoma rash?
cards.a: Necrolytic Migratory Erythema (presents in intertriginous areas).

cards.q: Hormone elevated in Carcinoid Syndrome?
cards.a: Serotonin (5-HIAA in urine).

cards.q: Clinical symptoms of Carcinoid Syndrome?
cards.a: Flushing, diarrhea, and right-sided heart valve lesions.

cards.q: Why does Carcinoid Syndrome usually require liver metastasis?
cards.a: Primary tumor secretions are normally metabolized by the liver (first-pass). Section 16: Endocrine Hypertension & Renovascular

cards.q: Screening test for Renal Artery Stenosis?
cards.a: Renal Duplex Ultrasound or CT/MR Angiography.

cards.q: Effect of Renal Artery Stenosis on Renin and Aldosterone?
cards.a: High Renin, High Aldosterone (Secondary Hyperaldosteronism).

cards.q: Most common cause of Renal Artery Stenosis in young women?
cards.a: Fibromuscular Dysplasia.

cards.q: Most common cause of Renal Artery Stenosis in elderly men?
cards.a: Atherosclerosis.

cards.q: Classic finding in Fibromuscular Dysplasia on angiography?
cards.a: "String of beads" appearance of the renal artery.

cards.q: Why are ACE inhibitors contraindicated in bilateral Renal Artery Stenosis?
cards.a: They can cause acute renal failure by reducing efferent arteriolar tone/filtration pressure. Section 17: Rare Endocrine Tumors & Syndromes

cards.q: Clinical presentation of Insulinoma?
cards.a: Whipple’s Triad: Symptoms of hypoglycemia, low blood glucose, and relief of symptoms with glucose.

cards.q: C-peptide levels in Insulinoma vs. Exogenous Insulin use?
cards.a: Elevated in Insulinoma; Low/Suppressed in Exogenous Insulin use.

cards.q: Diagnosis of Somatostatinoma?
cards.a: Triad of Diabetes, Cholelithiasis (gallstones), and Steatorrhea.

cards.q: Primary symptom of a Gastrinoma (Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome)?
cards.a: Multiple, refractory, or distal peptic ulcers and chronic diarrhea.

cards.q: Best initial test for Gastrinoma?
cards.a: Fasting serum gastrin level (>1000 pg/mL is diagnostic).

cards.q: Secretin Stimulation Test result in Gastrinoma?
cards.a: Paradoxical increase in serum gastrin levels. Section 18: Pediatric & Pubertal Transitions (Internal Medicine Prep)

cards.q: Definition of Delayed Puberty in boys?
cards.a: Absence of testicular enlargement (volume < 4mL) by age 14.

cards.q: Definition of Delayed Puberty in girls?
cards.a: Absence of breast development (Thelarche) by age 13.

cards.q: Most common cause of Constitutional Delay of Growth and Puberty?
cards.a: Genetic/Familial (delayed "bone age" matches height age rather than chronological age). Section 19: Advanced Electrolytes & Hormone Interactions

cards.q: Effect of Hypomagnesemia on Potassium levels?
cards.a: Refractory Hypokalemia (K+ cannot be corrected until Mg2+ is replaced).

cards.q: Effect of Hypomagnesemia on PTH secretion?
cards.a: Inhibits PTH secretion and causes end-organ resistance to PTH, leading to hypocalcemia.

cards.q: What is "Hungry Bone Syndrome"?
cards.a: Severe hypocalcemia and hypophosphatemia following parathyroidectomy in patients with high preoperative bone turnover.

cards.q: Medical management of Hypercalcemia of Malignancy (refractory to fluids)?
cards.a: IV Bisphosphonates (Zoledronic acid) or Denosumab. Section 20: Rapid-Fire Management "Next Steps"

cards.q: Next step for a patient with a "Cold" nodule on Thyroid Scan?
cards.a: Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA).

cards.q: Next step for a patient with a "Hot" nodule on Thyroid Scan?
cards.a: Evaluate for hyperthyroidism; rarely malignant.

cards.q: Management of a pregnant patient with Hyperthyroidism?
cards.a: PTU in 1st trimester; Methimazole in 2nd and 3rd trimesters.

cards.q: Preferred imaging for localized Pheochromocytoma?
cards.a: CT or MRI of the abdomen/pelvis.

cards.q: Imaging used if CT/MRI fails to find a suspected Pheochromocytoma?
cards.a: MIBG (Metaiodobenzylguanidine) scan.

cards.q: When to screen for Gestational Diabetes?
cards.a: Between 24 and 28 weeks of gestation.

cards.q: Initial treatment for Gestational Diabetes?
cards.a: Dietary modification and exercise.

cards.q: Preferred pharmacotherapy for Gestational Diabetes if lifestyle fails?
cards.a: Insulin (Metformin/Glyburide are second-line in some guidelines).

cards.q: Lab finding that distinguishes 21-Hydroxylase deficiency from 11-beta-Hydroxylase deficiency?
cards.a: 11-beta-Hydroxylase deficiency presents with Hypertension (due to 11-deoxycorticosterone).

cards.q: Major risk of over-replacing Levothyroxine in the elderly?
cards.a: Atrial fibrillation and bone mineral density loss. Final Synthesis: Clinical "Gems"

cards.q: Common cause of falsely low HbA1c?
cards.a: Conditions with high red blood cell turnover (e.g., Hemolytic Anemia, EPO therapy).

cards.q: Common cause of falsely high HbA1c?
cards.a: Iron deficiency anemia (longer RBC lifespan).

cards.q: What is the "Rule of 1s" for Addison's crisis?
cards.a: 1 liter of NS every 1 hour, plus 100mg Hydrocortisone.

cards.q: Primary hormonal deficiency in a patient with Pituitary Stalk Transection?
cards.a: All pituitary hormones decrease EXCEPT Prolactin (which increases due to loss of dopamine inhibition).

cards.q: What is "Apoplectic" presentation?
cards.a: Sudden onset of "worst headache of life," visual field defects, and ophthalmoplegia.

cards.q: Target HbA1c for most non-pregnant adults with DM2?
Primary reason to use Eplerenone over Spironolactone?
cards.a: Avoidance of anti-androgenic side effects like gynecomastia.

cards.q: Diagnostic test for Acromegaly after IGF-1 is found elevated?
cards.a: Glucose suppression test (GH should drop below 1 ng/mL after glucose load). Section 21: Complex Metabolic & Electrolyte Nuances

cards.q: What is the "Hooks Effect" in Prolactinoma testing?
cards.a: Extremely high prolactin levels can saturate the lab assay, leading to a falsely low report; requires sample dilution.

cards.q: Serum Calcium and Phosphorus levels in Vitamin D-Resistant Rickets (X-linked hypophosphatemia)?
cards.a: Normal Calcium, Low Phosphorus, and Low/Normal Vitamin D ($1,25,OH_2D$).

cards.q: Primary hormonal abnormality in Gitelman Syndrome?
cards.a: Mimics Thiazide diuretic use (Hypokalemia, Metabolic Alkalosis, Hypomagnesemia, and Hypocalciuria).

cards.q: Primary hormonal abnormality in Bartter Syndrome?
cards.a: Mimics Loop diuretic use (Hypokalemia, Metabolic Alkalosis, and Hypercalciuria).

cards.q: Definition of "Schmidt Syndrome" (APS Type 2)?
cards.a: Adrenal insufficiency + Autoimmune thyroid disease + Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus. Section 22: Advanced Pharmacology & Interactions

cards.q: Effect of Cholestyramine on Levothyroxine absorption?
cards.a: Decreases absorption; Levothyroxine should be taken 4 hours apart from bile acid sequestrants.

cards.q: Mechanism of Denosumab?
cards.a: Monoclonal antibody against RANKL, inhibiting osteoclast maturation.

cards.q: Mechanism of Cinacalcet?
cards.a: Calcimimetic that increases the sensitivity of calcium-sensing receptors on the parathyroid gland to suppress PTH.

cards.q: Why is Pioglitazone avoided in patients with a history of bladder cancer?
cards.a: Potential increased risk of bladder malignancy.

cards.q: Major side effect of Mitotane?
cards.a: Adrenolytic effect used to treat adrenal cortex carcinoma; causes severe GI distress and CNS depression. Section 23: Rare Syndromes & Pathophysiology

cards.q: Clinical presentation of Klinefelter Syndrome at puberty?
cards.a: Gynecomastia, sparse body hair, and "firm" small testes (testicular dysgenesis).

cards.q: Hormonal profile of Turner Syndrome (45, X)?
cards.a: Primary ovarian failure leading to high FSH and LH (Hypergonadotropic Hypogonadism).

cards.q: Most common cause of "Precocious Puberty" in boys?
cards.a: CNS tumors (e.g., hypothalamic hamartoma).

cards.q: Most common cause of "Precocious Puberty" in girls?
cards.a: Idiopathic (early activation of the HPO axis).

cards.q: What is "Liddle Syndrome"?
cards.a: Genetic mutation causing overactive ENaC channels; presents as hypertension, hypokalemia, and suppressed renin/aldosterone. Section 24: Critical "Next Best Step" Scenarios

cards.q: Next step in a patient with suspected Pheochromocytoma and a family history of Medullary Thyroid Cancer?
cards.a: Genetic testing for RET proto-oncogene (MEN 2).

cards.q: Next step for a patient with symptomatic Hypercalcemia and a suppressed PTH?
cards.a: Measure PTHrP, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, and SPEP (screen for malignancy/sarcoid).

cards.q: Next step for a patient with new-onset Diabetes and high Ferritin levels?
cards.a: Genetic testing for HFE gene (Hereditary Hemochromatosis/Bronze Diabetes).

cards.q: Management of a patient with an LDL > 190 mg/dL?
cards.a: Immediate initiation of High-intensity Statin therapy regardless of 10-year risk score.

cards.q: Preferred treatment for a pregnant patient with Prolactinoma?
cards.a: Discontinue Dopamine agonists; monitor for visual field changes. Section 25: The "Ridiculously Simple" Review

cards.q: Classic "Stone, Moans, Groans, and Psychic Overtones" refers to?
cards.a: Clinical symptoms of Hypercalcemia.

cards.q: Mnemonic for the causes of a "High Anion Gap" in Endocrinology?
cards.a: MUDPILES (specifically "D" for Diabetic Ketoacidosis).

cards.q: Why does Primary Hypothyroidism sometimes cause Hyperprolactinemia?
cards.a: High TRH acts as a weak prolactin-releasing factor.

cards.q: Characteristic of "Watery Diarrhea" in VIPoma?
cards.a: Persists even during fasting (secretory diarrhea).

cards.q: What is "Ertl’s sign"?
cards.a: A rare physical sign (thyroid bruits) sometimes heard in Graves disease. Section 26: Diagnostic Thresholds Recap

cards.q: Minimum diameter for a thyroid nodule to warrant FNA if it has "high-risk" ultrasound features?
cards.a: $\ge 1$ cm.

cards.q: Fasting glucose level defining "Impaired Fasting Glucose"?
cards.a: 100 mg/dL to 125 mg/dL.

cards.q: Random blood glucose level + symptoms required for DM diagnosis?
cards.a: $\ge 200$ mg/dL.

cards.q: Normal range for 24-hour urinary free cortisol?
cards.a: < 90 mcg/day (varies slightly by lab, but high-yield for "normal" cutoffs).

cards.q: Urine osmolality in a patient with Primary Polydipsia?
cards.a: Low (< 100 mOsm/kg), as the kidneys are maximally diluting urine to excrete water. Section 27: Hormone Resistance & Genetic Variants

cards.q: Cause of Pseudohypoparathyroidism Type 1a?
cards.a: Defect in the Gs-protein alpha subunit (maternal inheritance).

cards.q: Phenotype of Albright Hereditary Osteodystrophy?
cards.a: Short stature, round face, short 4th and 5th metacarpals, and subcutaneous calcifications.

cards.q: Lab profile of Vitamin D-dependent Rickets Type II?
cards.a: High 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D levels due to vitamin D receptor resistance.

cards.q: Clinical sign of Severe Insulin Resistance (Type A)?
cards.a: Severe Acanthosis Nigricans and virilization in young women.

cards.q: Difference between MODY (Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young) and Type 2 DM?
cards.a: MODY is autosomal dominant, occurs in non-obese young patients, and is due to a single gene defect in beta-cell function. Section 28: Paraneoplastic & Ectopic Endocrine Syndromes

cards.q: Most common cause of Ectopic ACTH production?
cards.a: Small Cell Lung Cancer.

cards.q: Paraneoplastic cause of Hypercalcemia in Squamous Cell Lung Cancer?
cards.a: PTH-related protein (PTHrP) production.

cards.q: Endocrine cause of Erythrocytosis (high Hgb/Hct)?
cards.a: Pheochromocytoma or Cushing’s Syndrome (due to EPO-like effects or cortisol's marrow stimulation).

cards.q: Syndrome associated with Primary Adrenal Lymphoma?
cards.a: Bilateral adrenal enlargement and primary adrenal insufficiency. Section 29: Thyroid & Metabolic Nuances

cards.q: Result of a Perchlorate Discharge Test?
cards.a: Identifies defects in thyroid iodine organification.

cards.q: Definition of "Pemberton’s Sign"?
cards.a: Facial flushing and neck vein distension when raising arms, indicating a large substernal goiter.

cards.q: Serum marker that is elevated in Thyroid Lymphoma?
cards.a: Anti-TPO antibodies (often arises in the background of Hashimoto's).

cards.q: Preferred management for a "toxic" (hyperfunctioning) thyroid nodule?
cards.a: Radioactive Iodine Ablation or Surgery (Methimazole is usually bridge therapy). Section 30: Advanced Lipidology & Metabolism

cards.q: Characteristic finding in Type III Dysbetalipoproteinemia?
cards.a: Palmar xanthomas and elevations in IDL (Intermediate-Density Lipoprotein).

cards.q: Genetic defect in Type III Dysbetalipoproteinemia?
cards.a: ApoE-2 homozygosity (results in decreased clearance of chylomicron remnants).

cards.q: Effect of high-dose Glucocorticoids on Calcium metabolism?
cards.a: Decreases intestinal calcium absorption and increases renal calcium excretion (leads to osteoporosis).

cards.q: Primary cause of death in untreated Primary Hyperparathyroidism?
cards.a: Actually usually unrelated to the PTH; however, severe "Hypercalcemic Crisis" can lead to cardiac arrest. Section 31: Specific Drug-Induced Endocrine Changes

cards.q: Effect of Spironolactone on Testosterone?
cards.a: Competitively inhibits the androgen receptor and decreases testosterone synthesis (causes gynecomastia).

cards.q: Medication that can cause both Hypothyroidism and Hyperthyroidism?
cards.a: Amiodarone (due to high iodine content).

cards.q: Effect of Phenytoin/Rifampin on Vitamin D metabolism?
cards.a: Induces P450 enzymes, leading to increased catabolism of Vitamin D and potential osteomalacia.

cards.q: Why is Radioiodine therapy contraindicated in Graves' patients with severe Ophthalmopathy?
cards.a: It can acutely worsen the eye disease by increasing TSH-receptor antibody titers. Section 32: The "Last Look" USMLE Pearls

cards.q: Most common cause of Primary Hyperparathyroidism in a patient with MEN 1?
cards.a: Parathyroid Hyperplasia (multiglandular) rather than a single adenoma.

cards.q: Diagnostic test for suspected Cushing's in a patient with Renal Failure?
cards.a: Late-night salivary cortisol (24-hour urine cortisol is unreliable in renal failure).

cards.q: Preferred steroid for replacement in Addison’s to mimic natural rhythm?
cards.a: Hydrocortisone (divided doses, 2/3 in morning, 1/3 in afternoon).

cards.q: Requirement for adding Fludrocortisone in Adrenal Insufficiency?
cards.a: Only needed in Primary Adrenal Insufficiency (to replace Mineralocorticoids).

cards.q: Clinical presentation of "Apathetic Hyperthyroidism"?
cards.a: Depression, lethargy, and weight loss in elderly patients with thyrotoxicosis (missing the usual "hyper" symptoms).

cards.q: Definition of "Wolff-Chaikoff Effect"?
cards.a: Reduction in thyroid hormone levels caused by the ingestion of a large amount of iodine.

cards.q: Definition of "Jod-Basedow Phenomenon"?
cards.a: Iodine-induced hyperthyroidism in a patient with a pre-existing multinodular goiter. Section 33: Enzymatic Deficiencies (CAH Variations)

cards.q: Characteristic finding in 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency?
cards.a: Hypertension and Hypokalemia with female phenotype (or undescended testes in males).

cards.q: Primary steroid excess in 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency?
cards.a: 11-deoxycorticosterone (leads to hypertension).

cards.q: Distinguishing feature between 21-hydroxylase and 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency?
cards.a: 21-hydroxylase deficiency causes hypotension; 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency causes hypertension.

cards.q: Primary hormone deficiency in 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase deficiency?
cards.a: Deficiency of all adrenal and gonadal steroid hormones. Section 34: Hypoglycemia & Non-Diabetes Pancreatic Issues

cards.q: Diagnosis of Non-insulinoma Pancreatogenous Hypoglycemia Syndrome (NIPHS)?
cards.a: Postprandial hypoglycemia caused by beta-cell hypertrophy (not a tumor).

cards.q: Mechanism of Factitious Hypoglycemia via Sulfonylurea?
cards.a: Elevated Insulin and elevated C-peptide (mimics Insulinoma; requires urine drug screen).

cards.q: What is the "72-hour fast" used for?
cards.a: The gold standard for diagnosing Insulinoma in a controlled inpatient setting.

cards.q: Treatment for symptomatic hypoglycemia in a patient with an Inoperable Insulinoma?
cards.a: Diazoxide (inhibits insulin secretion) or Octreotide. Section 35: Metabolic Bone Disease Fine-Tuning

cards.q: Effect of Hyperthyroidism on bone metabolism?
cards.a: Increased bone resorption leading to hypercalciuria and potentially osteoporosis.

cards.q: Lab finding in Hypophosphatemic Rickets?
cards.a: Low serum phosphorus with inappropriately low or normal 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D.

cards.q: Why is Vitamin D supplementation essential in Hypoparathyroidism?
cards.a: Lack of PTH prevents the conversion of 25-OH Vitamin D to its active 1,25-OH form.

cards.q: Radiographic sign of Scurvy (Vitamin C deficiency) in children?
cards.a: Wimberger’s ring sign (circular calcification around the epiphyseal center). Section 36: Neuroendocrinology & Sleep

cards.q: Effect of Sleep Apnea on the endocrine system?
cards.a: Can cause secondary polycythemia and is highly associated with insulin resistance/Type 2 DM.

cards.q: Hormone secreted by the Pineal Gland?
cards.a: Melatonin.

cards.q: Effect of Craniopharyngioma on growth in children?
cards.a: Growth failure due to Growth Hormone Deficiency (pituitary compression). Section 37: Endocrine Changes in Systemic Disease

cards.q: Endocrine manifestation of Sarcoidosis?
cards.a: Hypercalcemia (due to 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity in macrophages) and Central Diabetes Insipidus.

cards.q: Endocrine manifestation of Hemochromatosis?
cards.a: Central Hypogonadism (iron deposition in pituitary) and "Bronze" Diabetes (pancreatic deposition).

cards.q: Common endocrine side effect of Checkpoint Inhibitors (Immunotherapy)?
cards.a: Hypophysitis (inflammation of the pituitary gland). Section 38: Pregnancy & Reproductive Nuances

cards.q: Effect of Pregnancy on Total T4 and T3?
cards.a: Increases due to high Estrogen-induced Thyroid Binding Globulin (TBG).

cards.q: Why is hCG able to stimulate the Thyroid gland?
cards.a: The alpha-subunit of hCG is identical to TSH.

cards.q: Definition of "Postpartum Thyroiditis"?
cards.a: Autoimmune thyroiditis occurring within 1 year of delivery; usually transient hyperthyroid followed by hypothyroid.

cards.q: Management of Gestational Hypothyroidism?
cards.a: Aggressive Levothyroxine replacement; requirements often increase by 30–50% during pregnancy. Section 39: The "Differential" Master List

cards.q: Differential for a "Low TSH, Low Free T4"?
cards.a: Central (Secondary) Hypothyroidism or Euthyroid Sick Syndrome.

cards.q: Differential for "High PTH, High Calcium"?
cards.a: Primary Hyperparathyroidism or Familial Hypocalciuric Hypercalcemia (FHH).

cards.q: How to distinguish FHH from Primary Hyperparathyroidism?
cards.a: FHH has a low 24-hour urinary calcium excretion (UCCE < 0.01).

cards.q: Differential for "Low PTH, High Calcium"?
cards.a: Malignancy, Vitamin D toxicity, or Sarcoidosis.

cards.q: Differential for "High PTH, Low Calcium"?
cards.a: Secondary Hyperparathyroidism (usually CKD or Vitamin D deficiency) or Pseudohypoparathyroidism. Section 40: "Ridiculously Simple" Clinical Logic

cards.q: Why do we treat Hyperkalemia with Insulin and Glucose?
cards.a: Insulin drives potassium into the cells by stimulating the Na+/K+ ATPase pump.

cards.q: Mnemonic for MEN 1?
cards.a: The 3 Ps: Pituitary, Parathyroid, Pancreas.

cards.q: Mnemonic for MEN 2A?
cards.a: The 1 M, 2 Ps: Medullary Thyroid, Pheochromocytoma, Parathyroid.

cards.q: Mnemonic for MEN 2B?
cards.a: The 2 Ms, 1 P: Medullary Thyroid, Marfanoid Habitus/Mucosal Neuromas, Pheochromocytoma. Section 41: Endocrine Oncology & Genetic Markers

cards.q: Screening test for family members of a patient with Medullary Thyroid Cancer?
cards.a: DNA testing for RET proto-oncogene mutations.

cards.q: Serum marker used to monitor treatment response in Carcinoid tumors?
cards.a: Chromogranin A.

cards.q: Most common site for an extra-adrenal Pheochromocytoma (Paraganglioma)?
cards.a: The Organ of Zuckerkandl (near the aortic bifurcation).

cards.q: Diagnostic test for suspected Cushing's when initial screening is equivocal?
cards.a: Inferior Petrosal Sinus Sampling (IPSS) to distinguish pituitary vs. ectopic source.

cards.q: Hormone typically secreted by a "non-functioning" pituitary adenoma?
cards.a: Gonadotropins (specifically the alpha-subunit), though they rarely cause a clinical syndrome. Section 42: Specialized Management Nuances

cards.q: When is surgery (Parathyroidectomy) indicated for asymptomatic Primary Hyperparathyroidism?
cards.a: Age < 50, Calcium > 1.0 mg/dL above normal, T-score < -2.5, or GFR < 60.

cards.q: Initial medical management for a patient with a known VIPoma?
cards.a: Octreotide (to control diarrhea) and aggressive fluid/electrolyte replacement.

cards.q: Preferred treatment for "Toxic Multinodular Goiter"?
cards.a: Radioactive Iodine (131-I) or surgery (methimazole is not a definitive cure).

cards.q: First-line management for Central Diabetes Insipidus?
cards.a: Desmopressin (DDAVP), available in oral, nasal, or parenteral forms.

cards.q: First-line management for Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus?
cards.a: HCTZ (Thiazide diuretics), NSAIDs, and a low-salt diet. Section 43: Endocrine Emergencies (Detailed)

cards.q: Serum Glucose level diagnostic of "Hypoglycemia" in a non-diabetic patient?
cards.a: < 55 mg/dL with associated symptoms.

cards.q: Calculation for Serum Osmolality?
cards.a: $2 \times [Na^+] + \frac{Glucose}{18} + \frac{BUN}{2.8}$.

cards.q: First step in managing a patient with suspected Thyroid Storm?
cards.a: Propranolol (to control sympathetic overactivity).

cards.q: Management of Myxedema Coma?
cards.a: IV Levothyroxine ($T_4$), IV Liothyronine ($T_3$), and stress-dose Glucocorticoids.

cards.q: Why must Glucocorticoids be given before $T_4$ in Myxedema Coma?
cards.a: To prevent precipitating an adrenal crisis if the patient has co-existing adrenal insufficiency. Section 44: Reproductive & Gonadal Nuances

cards.q: Definition of "Primary Amenorrhea"?
cards.a: No menses by age 15 with secondary sex characteristics, or by age 13 without them.

cards.q: Most common cause of Primary Amenorrhea with a present uterus?
cards.a: Turner Syndrome (45, X).

cards.q: Most common cause of Primary Amenorrhea with an absent uterus?
cards.a: Müllerian Agenesis (Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome).

cards.q: Distinguishing feature of Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome (AIS) from Müllerian Agenesis?
cards.a: AIS has male-level testosterone and absent pubic/axillary hair.

cards.q: Hormone elevated in 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency but low in 21-hydroxylase deficiency?
cards.a: 11-deoxycorticosterone (DOC). Section 45: "Ridiculously Simple" Electrolyte Memory Hooks

cards.q: How does "Acidosis" affect ionized Calcium levels?
cards.a: Increases ionized Calcium (hydrogen ions displace calcium from albumin).

cards.q: How does "Alkalosis" affect ionized Calcium levels?
cards.a: Decreases ionized Calcium (leads to increased binding to albumin; can cause tetany).

cards.q: Mnemonic for the effects of Glucagon?
cards.a: GREAT: Glycogenolysis, Releases Insulin, Energy (fatty acid oxidation), Acetone (ketogenesis), Tops gluconeogenesis. Section 46: Chronic Disease & Endocrine Overlap

cards.q: Most common endocrine abnormality in patients with Thalassemia Major?
cards.a: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (due to iron overload in the pituitary).

cards.q: Endocrine association with Celiac Disease?
cards.a: Type 1 Diabetes and Autoimmune Thyroiditis (shared genetic predisposition).

cards.q: Why do patients with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) develop osteomalacia?
Most common cause of microcytic hypochromic anemia worldwide?
cards.a: Iron deficiency anemia.

cards.q: Initial and most sensitive lab test for diagnosing iron deficiency anemia?
cards.a: Serum ferritin level.

cards.q: Formula for Total Iron Binding Capacity (TIBC) relation to transferrin?
cards.a: TIBC is a direct measurement of serum transferrin levels.

cards.q: Pattern of serum iron and TIBC in iron deficiency anemia?
cards.a: Low serum iron and elevated TIBC.

cards.q: Pattern of serum iron and TIBC in Anemia of Chronic Disease (ACD)?
cards.a: Low serum iron and low or normal TIBC.

cards.q: Key inflammatory cytokine that mediates Anemia of Chronic Disease?
cards.a: Hepcidin.

cards.q: Mechanism by which hepcidin causes anemia of chronic disease?
cards.a: Binds to and degrades ferroportin, trapping iron inside macrophages and enterocytes.

cards.q: Microcytic anemia presenting with basophilic stippling and ringed sideroblasts?
cards.a: Lead poisoning.

cards.q: Enzyme inhibited by lead that leads to accumulation of protoporphyrin?
cards.a: Ferrochelatase (and ALA dehydratase).

cards.q: Definitve diagnostic test to distinguish Thalassemia trait from Iron Deficiency Anemia?
cards.a: Hemoglobin electrophoresis.

cards.q: Hemoglobin electrophoresis profile characteristic of Beta-Thalassemia minor?
cards.a: Elevated $HbA_2$ ($>3.5\%$) and slightly elevated HbF.

cards.q: Chromosome location of the alpha-globin genes?
cards.a: Chromosome 16.

cards.q: Chromosome location of the beta-globin genes?
cards.a: Chromosome 11.

cards.q: Clinical manifestation of a 3-alpha-globin gene deletion alpha-thalassemia?
cards.a: Hemoglobin H (HbH) disease, causing chronic hemolytic anemia.

cards.q: Composition of Hemoglobin H (HbH)?
cards.a: Tetramers of beta-globin ($\beta_4$).

cards.q: Clinical manifestation of a 4-alpha-globin gene deletion alpha-thalassemia?
cards.a: Hydrops fetalis (Hemoglobin Barts).

cards.q: Composition of Hemoglobin Barts?
cards.a: Tetramers of gamma-globin ($\gamma_4$).

cards.q: Classic skull X-ray finding in Beta-Thalassemia major due to extramedullary hematopoiesis?
cards.a: "Crew-cut" appearance (hair-on-end). Macrocytic and Normocytic Anemias

cards.q: Distinctive peripheral blood smear finding that differentiates megaloblastic from non-megaloblastic macrocytic anemia?
cards.a: Hypersegmented neutrophils ($>5$ lobes).

cards.q: Metabolic product that builds up in Vitamin B12 deficiency but NOT in folate deficiency?
cards.a: Methylmalonic acid (MMA).

cards.q: Spinal cord pathology associated with severe Vitamin B12 deficiency?
cards.a: Subacute Combined Degeneration (SCD) of the spinal cord.

cards.q: Specific anatomical site of dietary Vitamin B12 absorption?
cards.a: Terminal ileum.

cards.q: Glycoprotein required for Vitamin B12 absorption that is deficient in pernicious anemia?
cards.a: Intrinsic Factor (IF).

cards.q: Primary site of dietary folate absorption?
cards.a: Jejunum.

cards.q: Classic triad of Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH)?
cards.a: Hemolytic anemia, pancytopenia, and venous thrombosis.

cards.q: Flow cytometry findings diagnostic for Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH)?
cards.a: Absence of CD55 and CD59 on RBC surfaces.

cards.q: Mutated gene responsible for Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria?
cards.a: PIGA gene (phosphatidylinositol glycan anchor biosynthesis class A).

cards.q: Mode of inheritance for Hereditary Spherocytosis?
cards.a: Autosomal dominant.

cards.q: Most common molecular/protein defects in Hereditary Spherocytosis?
cards.a: Defects in ankyrin, spectrin, or band 3.

cards.q: Screening test of choice for diagnosing Hereditary Spherocytosis?
cards.a: Eosin-5-maleimide (EMA) binding test or osmotic fragility test.

cards.q: Definitive treatment to control hemolytic symptoms in Hereditary Spherocytosis?
cards.a: Splenectomy.

cards.q: Exact amino acid substitution that causes Sickle Cell Anemia?
cards.a: Glutamic acid to valine at position 6 of the beta-globin chain.

cards.q: Most common precipitating factor for a sickle cell vaso-occlusive crisis?
cards.a: Hypoxia, dehydration, or infection.

cards.q: Encapsulated organisms that autosplenectomized sickle cell patients are highly susceptible to?
cards.a: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and Haemophilus influenzae.

cards.q: Maintenance medication used in Sickle Cell Anemia to increase Hemoglobin F production?
cards.a: Hydroxyurea.

cards.q: Most common organism causing osteomyelitis in patients with Sickle Cell Disease?
cards.a: Salmonella species.

cards.q: Mode of inheritance for Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency?
cards.a: X-linked recessive.

cards.q: Two classic structures visualized on a peripheral blood smear during a G6PD crisis?
cards.a: Heinz bodies and bite cells.

cards.q: Diagnostic test used to differentiate Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia (AIHA) from hereditary hemolytic anemias?
cards.a: Direct Antiglobulin Test (DAT / Direct Coombs).

cards.q: Immunoglobulin type associated with Warm Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia?
cards.a: IgG.

cards.q: Immunoglobulin type associated with Cold Agglutinin Disease?
cards.a: IgM.

cards.q: Classic physical exam finding that differentiates Aplastic Anemia from leukemia or lymphoma?
cards.a: Absence of splenomegaly or lymphadenopathy.

cards.q: Bone marrow biopsy finding diagnostic for Aplastic Anemia?
cards.a: Hypocellular marrow replaced by fat cells. Acute Leukemias

cards.q: Minimum percentage of bone marrow blasts required to diagnose Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)?
cards.a: $20\%$ or greater.

cards.q: Pathognomonic crystalline cytoplasmic inclusion bodies found in AML blasts?
cards.a: Auer rods.

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation pathognomonic for Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL)?
Fusion gene product created by the $\text{t}(15;17)$ translocation?
cards.a: PML-RARA.

cards.q: Life-threatening coagulopathy frequently precipitated by Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia?
cards.a: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC).

cards.q: Targeted medical therapy used to induce differentiation of blasts in APL?
cards.a: All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) and arsenic trioxide.

cards.q: Histochemical stain used to differentiate AML blasts from ALL blasts?
cards.a: Myeloperoxidase (MPO) stain.

cards.q: Most common pediatric malignancy?
cards.a: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL).

cards.q: Cell surface markers/enzymes characteristic of lymphoblasts in ALL?
cards.a: Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT).

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation associated with a poor prognosis in adult B-cell ALL?
cards.a: $\text{t}(9;22)$ (Philadelphia chromosome).

cards.q: Prophylactic therapy required in all ALL treatment regimens to prevent relapse?
cards.a: Central Nervous System (CNS) prophylaxis (intrathecal chemotherapy). Chronic Myeloproliferative and Lymphoproliferative Disorders

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation present in $>95\%$ of Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML) cases?
Constitutively active tyrosine kinase fusion protein produced in CML?
cards.a: BCR-ABL1.

cards.q: First-line targeted therapy for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia?
cards.a: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (e.g., Imatinib, Dasatinib).

cards.q: Leukocyte Alkaline Phosphatase (LAP) score trend in CML vs. Leukemoid Reaction?
cards.a: Decreased in CML; elevated in Leukemoid Reaction.

cards.q: Terminal phase of CML characterized by $>20\%$ blasts in the blood or marrow?
cards.a: Blast crisis.

cards.q: Driver mutation found in $>95\%$ of cases of Polycythemia Vera?
cards.a: JAK2 V617F mutation.

cards.q: Classic pruritus symptom unique to Polycythemia Vera?
cards.a: Aquagenic pruritus (itching after a warm bath/shower).

cards.q: Primary therapeutic intervention to maintain hematocrit $<45\%$ in Polycythemia Vera?
cards.a: Therapeutic phlebotomy.

cards.q: Bone marrow biopsy feature hallmark of Primary Myelofibrosis?
cards.a: Extensive collagen fibrosis and megakaryocyte hyperplasia.

cards.q: Classic erythrocyte morphology seen on peripheral smear in Primary Myelofibrosis?
cards.a: Teardrop poikilocytes (dacrocytes).

cards.q: Most common leukemia of adults in Western countries?
cards.a: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL).

cards.q: Characteristic artifactual cell configuration seen on peripheral smear in CLL?
cards.a: Smudge cells.

cards.q: Immunophenotype co-expression pattern characteristic of CLL B-cells?
cards.a: CD5 and CD19/CD20/CD23.

cards.q: Name given to the transformation of CLL into an aggressive Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma?
cards.a: Richter transformation. Lymphomas

cards.q: Pathognomonic giant, multinucleated cell type seen in Hodgkin Lymphoma?
cards.a: Reed-Sternberg (RS) cell.

cards.q: Immunophenotype markers typically expressed by classic Reed-Sternberg cells?
cards.a: CD15 and CD30.

cards.q: Most common histological subtype of Hodgkin Lymphoma?
cards.a: Nodular sclerosis subtype.

cards.q: Constitutional symptoms designated as "B symptoms" in lymphoma staging?
cards.a: Fever, drenching night sweats, and unexplained weight loss ($>10\%$ in 6 months).

cards.q: Name of the staging system used for Hodgkin and Non-Hodgkin Lymphomas?
cards.a: Ann Arbor Staging System (or Lugano classification).

cards.q: Most common subtype of Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma worldwide?
cards.a: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL).

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation and gene associated with Burkitt Lymphoma?
cards.a: $\text{t}(8;14)$ causing c-myc overexpression.

cards.q: Characteristic histological description of a Burkitt Lymphoma biopsy?
cards.a: "Starry sky" appearance.

cards.q: Infection highly associated with endemic (African) Burkitt Lymphoma?
cards.a: Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV).

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation and gene associated with Follicular Lymphoma?
cards.a: $\text{t}(14;18)$ causing BCL-2 overexpression.

cards.q: Pathophysiological effect of BCL-2 overexpression in Follicular Lymphoma?
cards.a: Inhibition of apoptosis in B-cells.

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation and gene associated with Mantle Cell Lymphoma?
cards.a: $\text{t}(11;14)$ causing Cyclin D1 overexpression. Plasma Cell Dyscrasias

cards.q: Diagnostic criteria that differentiates Multiple Myeloma from MGUS?
cards.a: Clonal bone marrow plasma cells $\ge 10\%$ OR biopsy-proven plasmacytoma, plus CRAB features.

cards.q: Components of the acronym CRAB used in Multiple Myeloma diagnosis?
cards.a: HyperCalcemia, Renal insufficiency, Anemia, and Bone lytic lesions.

cards.q: Monoclonal protein production description in MGUS without end-organ damage?
cards.a: Serum M-protein $<3\text{ g/dL}$ and bone marrow plasma cells $<10\%$.

cards.q: RBC stacking phenomenon seen on peripheral smear in Multiple Myeloma?
cards.a: Rouleaux formation.

cards.q: Free light chains cleared by the kidney and found in the urine of Myeloma patients?
cards.a: Bence-Jones proteins.

cards.q: Classic skull X-ray finding in Multiple Myeloma?
cards.a: "Punched-out" lytic bone lesions.

cards.q: Triad defining Waldenström Macroglobulinemia?
cards.a: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma in marrow, monoclonal IgM spike, and hyperviscosity.

cards.q: Primary clinical presentation unique to Waldenström Macroglobulinemia due to IgM size?
cards.a: Hyperviscosity syndrome (visual changes, neurological symptoms, bleeding). Platelet Disorders and Coagulopathies

cards.q: Primary target of autoantibodies in Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP)?
cards.a: Platelet GP IIb/IIIa or GP Ib/IX receptors.

cards.q: First-line medical therapy for an adult with symptomatic ITP and platelets $<30,000$?
cards.a: Corticosteroids (or IVIG).

cards.q: Pentad of clinical findings in Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP)?
cards.a: Thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, fever, renal failure, neurological signs.

cards.q: Enzyme deficiency or autoantibody target responsible for TTP?
cards.a: ADAMTS13.

cards.q: Pathophysiological function of the ADAMTS13 enzyme?
cards.a: Cleaves ultra-large von Willebrand factor (vWF) multimers.

cards.q: Contraindicated treatment modality in TTP that can worsen thrombosis?
cards.a: Platelet transfusion.

cards.q: Essential first-line treatment for Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP)?
cards.a: Therapeutic plasma exchange (plasmapheresis).

cards.q: Triad characterizing Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS)?
cards.a: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury.

cards.q: Most common infectious trigger for typical HUS in children?
cards.a: Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC, O157:H7).

cards.q: Most common inherited bleeding disorder?
cards.a: von Willebrand Disease (vWD).

cards.q: Dual function of von Willebrand Factor in hemostasis?
cards.a: Mediates platelet adhesion to subendothelium and stabilizes Factor VIII.

cards.q: Pattern of coagulation studies (PT/aPTT/Bleeding Time) in von Willebrand Disease?
cards.a: Normal PT, normal or prolonged aPTT, prolonged bleeding time (or abnormal PFA-100).

cards.q: Initial medical treatment used to elevate endogenous vWF and Factor VIII levels?
cards.a: Desmopressin (DDAVP).

cards.q: Coagulation factor deficiency in Hemophilia A?
cards.a: Factor VIII deficiency.

cards.q: Coagulation factor deficiency in Hemophilia B?
cards.a: Factor IX deficiency.

cards.q: Mode of inheritance for Hemophilia A and B?
cards.a: X-linked recessive.

cards.q: Classic clinical bleeding manifestation of severe hemophilia?
cards.a: Hemarthrosis (bleeding into joints).

cards.q: Coagulation profile (PT, aPTT, Platelets) for Hemophilia A or B?
cards.a: Prolonged aPTT, normal PT, normal platelet count.

cards.q: Diagnostic mixing study result if prolonged aPTT is due to factor deficiency?
cards.a: The aPTT corrects to normal when mixed 1:1 with normal plasma.

cards.q: Diagnostic mixing study result if prolonged aPTT is due to a factor inhibitor?
cards.a: The aPTT does not correct when mixed 1:1 with normal plasma.

cards.q: Classic lab profile of Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)?
cards.a: Prolonged PT, prolonged aPTT, decreased platelets, decreased fibrinogen, elevated D-dimer. Hypercoagulable States (Thrombophilia)

cards.q: Most common inherited hypercoagulable state among Caucasians?
cards.a: Factor V Leiden.

cards.q: Molecular mechanism of Factor V Leiden mutation?
cards.a: Single nucleotide mutation rendering Factor V resistant to inactivation by Activated Protein C (APC).

cards.q: Molecular mechanism of the Prothrombin G20210A mutation?
cards.a: Mutation in the 3' untranslated region leading to increased prothrombin levels.

cards.q: Dermatological complication that can occur when initiating Warfarin without heparin bridging?
cards.a: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis.

cards.q: Inherited thrombophilias that increase risk for warfarin-induced skin necrosis?
cards.a: Protein C or Protein S deficiency.

cards.q: Target of autoantibodies in Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS)?
cards.a: Lupus anticoagulant, Anticardiolipin antibodies, or Anti-beta2-glycoprotein I antibodies.

cards.q: Paradoxical laboratory finding in patients with Antiphospholipid Syndrome?
cards.a: Prolonged in vitro aPTT that does not correct with mixing studies, despite in vivo thrombosis. Transfusion Medicine & Complications

cards.q: Acute transfusion reaction characterized by fever, chills, and flank pain due to ABO incompatibility?
cards.a: Acute Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction.

cards.q: Cause of Febrile Non-Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction?
cards.a: Cytokines accumulated in the stored blood product during storage.

cards.q: Primary preventive strategy to avoid Febrile Non-Hemolytic Transfusion Reactions?
cards.a: Leukoreduction of blood products.

cards.q: Pulmonary transfusion complication presenting with hypoxemia and non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema within 6 hours?
cards.a: Transfusion-Related Acute Lung Injury (TRALI).

cards.q: Pathophysiology driving Transfusion-Related Acute Lung Injury (TRALI)?
cards.a: Donor antibodies targeting recipient neutrophils in the pulmonary vasculature.

cards.q: Pulmonary transfusion complication presenting with hypoxemia, hypertension, and jugular venous distention?
cards.a: Transfusion-Associated Circulatory Overload (TACO).

cards.q: Delayed transfusion reaction occurring days to weeks later, presenting with mild jaundice and falling hemoglobin?
cards.a: 状况 Delayed Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction.

cards.q: Primary mechanism behind Delayed Hemolytic Transfusion Reactions?
cards.a: Anamnestic antibody response against minor RBC antigens (e.g., Kidd, Kell). Myelodysplastic Syndromes and Bone Marrow Failure

cards.q: Pathognomonic bone marrow finding in Myelodysplastic Syndrome (MDS) showing a ring of iron deposits around the nucleus?
cards.a: Ringed sideroblast.

cards.q: Distinctive bi-lobed neutrophil morphology ("sunglasses appearance") classic for Myelodysplastic Syndrome?
cards.a: Pelger-Huët anomaly.

cards.q: Most common cytogenetic deletion associated with a specific, favorable-prognosis subtype of MDS?
cards.a: 5q deletion (5q- syndrome).

cards.q: Targeted medical therapy of choice for transfusion-dependent patients with 5q- Myelodysplastic Syndrome?
cards.a: Lenalidomide.

cards.q: Inherited bone marrow failure syndrome presenting with aplastic anemia, short stature, absent thumbs, and café-au-lait spots?
cards.a: Fanconi Anemia.

cards.q: Definitive diagnostic screening test for Fanconi Anemia?
cards.a: Chromosome breakage analysis (using diepoxybutane or mitomycin C).

cards.q: Inherited pure red cell aplasia presenting in infancy with craniofacial abnormalities and triphalangeal thumbs?
cards.a: Diamond-Blackfan Anemia. Hemolytic and Hemoglobinopathic Nuances

cards.q: Mechanism of RBC destruction in Warm Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia?
cards.a: Splenic macrophages pit the IgG-coated membrane, causing extravascular hemolysis and spherocyte formation.

cards.q: Mechanism of RBC destruction in Cold Agglutinin Disease?
cards.a: IgM binds RBCs in the cold, fixes complement, and C3b-coated RBCs are destroyed by hepatic Kupffer cells.

cards.q: Two classic infections that characteristically precipitate Cold Agglutinin Disease?
cards.a: Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV).

cards.q: Primary therapeutic choice for severe, symptomatic Warm Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia?
cards.a: Corticosteroids (or Rituximab).

cards.q: First-line management strategy for Cold Agglutinin Disease that avoids immunosuppressants?
cards.a: Avoidance of cold temperatures.

cards.q: Most common presentation of Sickle Cell Trait (heterozygous HbAS) on routine urinalysis?
cards.a: Microscopic hematuria (due to focal sickling in the renal medulla).

cards.q: Phenomenon causing acute, profound drop in hemoglobin in sickle cell patients, associated with a reticulocytopenia?
cards.a: Aplastic crisis.

cards.q: Most common viral pathogen responsible for triggering an aplastic crisis in sickle cell or hereditary spherocytosis patients?
cards.a: Parvovirus B19.

cards.q: Phenomenon causing an acute drop in hemoglobin in sickle cell patients, associated with splenomegaly and reticulocytosis?
cards.a: Splenic sequestration crisis.

cards.q: Leading cause of death in adult patients with Sickle Cell Disease?
cards.a: Acute Chest Syndrome.

cards.q: Diagnostic criteria for Acute Chest Syndrome in a sickle cell patient?
cards.a: New pulmonary infiltrate on chest X-ray plus fever, chest pain, tachypnea, or hypoxia. Advanced Leukemia and Lymphoma Concepts

cards.q: Genetic mutation found in nearly all cases of Hairy Cell Leukemia?
cards.a: BRAF V600E mutation.

cards.q: Key histochemical stain historically used to identify Hairy Cell Leukemia cells?
cards.a: Tartrate-Resistant Acid Phosphatase (TRAP) stain.

cards.q: Preferred highly effective first-line purine analog therapy for Hairy Cell Leukemia?
cards.a: Cladribine (2-chlorodeoxyadenosine).

cards.q: Classic physical exam finding characteristically ABSENT in Hairy Cell Leukemia despite massive splenomegaly?
cards.a: Lymphadenopathy.

cards.q: The single most important prognostic factor for patients diagnosed with Hodgkin Lymphoma?
cards.a: Stage of the disease at the time of diagnosis.

cards.q: Unique physical symptom where lymph nodes become painful specifically after drinking alcohol?
cards.a: Alcohol-induced nodal pain in Hodgkin Lymphoma.

cards.q: Lymphoma subtype characterized by a "waxy," painless lymphadenopathy that fluctuates in size over years?
cards.a: Follicular Lymphoma.

cards.q: Histological finding that differentiates Follicular Lymphoma from benign reactive follicular hyperplasia?
cards.a: Monoclonal B-cell population and absence of tingible body macrophages in the follicles.

cards.q: Aggressive T-cell lymphoma presenting with lytic bone lesions, hypercalcemia, skin lesions, and "cloverleaf" T-cells?
cards.a: Adult T-Cell Leukemia/Lymphoma (ATLL).

cards.q: Causative viral pathogen direct linked to Adult T-Cell Leukemia/Lymphoma?
cards.a: Human T-Cell Leukemia Virus type 1 (HTLV-1).

cards.q: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma characterized by cerebriform nuclei and skin plaques?
cards.a: Mycosis Fungoides.

cards.q: Term used when Mycosis Fungoides leukemizes, presenting with erythroderma and malignant T-cells in the peripheral blood?
cards.a: Sézary Syndrome. Coagulation, Anticoagulation, and Platelet Pathology

cards.q: Laboratory marker used to monitor the therapeutic efficacy and dosing of Unfractionated Heparin?
cards.a: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT).

cards.q: Laboratory marker used to monitor the therapeutic efficacy and dosing of Warfarin?
cards.a: Prothrombin Time (PT) / International Normalized Ratio (INR).

cards.q: Antidote used for the immediate reversal of Unfractionated Heparin?
cards.a: Protamine sulfate.

cards.q: Specific reversal agent for the Direct Oral Anticoagulant (DOAC) Dabigatran?
cards.a: Idarucizumab.

cards.q: Specific reversal agent for Factor Xa inhibitors (Rivaroxaban, Apixaban)?
cards.a: Andexanet alfa.

cards.q: Pathophysiological mechanism behind Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT)?
