cards.a: IgG antibodies form against the Heparin-Platelet Factor 4 (PF4) complex, activating platelets.

cards.q: Standard alternative anticoagulant of choice when HIT is confirmed or highly suspected?
cards.a: Direct thrombin inhibitors (e.g., Argatroban, Bivalirudin).

cards.q: Most accurate confirmatory laboratory assay for Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia?
cards.a: Serotonin Release Assay (SRA).

cards.q: Inherited condition presenting with prolonged bleeding time, normal platelet count, and giant platelets due to GP Ib-IX-V defect?
cards.a: Bernard-Soulier Syndrome.

cards.q: Inherited condition presenting with prolonged bleeding time, normal platelet count, and defective platelet aggregation due to GP IIb/IIIa defect?
cards.a: Glanzmann Thrombasthenia.

cards.q: Distinguishing aggregation assay result between Bernard-Soulier and Glanzmann Thrombasthenia?
cards.a: Ristocetin agglutination fixes Bernard-Soulier but does not correct Glanzmann; normal plasma corrects neither.

cards.q: Rare, life-threatening manifestation of severe DIC or meningococcemia presenting with bilateral adrenal hemorrhage and shock?
cards.a: Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome. Oncological Emergencies and Support

cards.q: Metabolic triad and secondary complication defining Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS)?
cards.a: Hyperuricemia, hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, and hypocalcemia.

cards.q: Mechanism by which Tumor Lysis Syndrome induces acute kidney injury?
cards.a: Precipitation of uric acid or calcium phosphate crystals in the renal tubules.

cards.q: Prophylactic medication used to prevent Tumor Lysis Syndrome by inhibiting xanthine oxidase?
cards.a: Allopurinol.

cards.q: Recombinant uric acid oxidase enzyme used to treat established, severe hyperuricemia in TLS?
cards.a: Rasburicase.

cards.q: Absolute Neutrophil Count (ANC) threshold used to define severe neutropenia?
cards.a: $\text{ANC} < 500/\mu\text{L}$.

cards.q: Empiric monotherapy antibiotic class required immediately in a patient with febrile neutropenia?
cards.a: Antipseudomonal beta-lactam (e.g., Cefepime, Meropenem, Piperacillin/Tazobactam).

cards.q: Immediate medical management for a cancer patient presenting with thoracic back pain, hyperreflexia, and lower extremity weakness?
cards.a: Intravenous high-dose corticosteroids (followed by emergent MRI for spinal cord compression).

cards.q: Pathophysiology behind Leukostasis Syndrome in patients with ultra-high WBC counts ($>100,000/\mu\text{L}$)?
cards.a: Increased blood viscosity and blast plugs causing tissue hypoxia, particularly in the brain and lungs. Iron Overload and Storage Disorders

cards.q: Classical triad of Hemochromatosis?
cards.a: Cirrhosis, diabetes mellitus ("bronze diabetes"), and skin hyperpigmentation.

cards.q: Most common genetic mutation associated with Hereditary Hemochromatosis?
cards.a: HFE gene mutation (C282Y or H63D).

cards.q: Transmembrane protein that is mutated or non-functional in Juvenile Hemochromatosis?
cards.a: Hemojuvelin or Hepcidin.

cards.q: Best screening lab evaluation for Hereditary Hemochromatosis?
cards.a: Transferrin saturation ($>45\%$) and serum ferritin.

cards.q: First-line management strategy for symptomatic Hereditary Hemochromatosis?
cards.a: Therapeutic phlebotomy.

cards.q: Preferred iron chelation therapy used for secondary iron overload due to chronic transfusions?
cards.a: Deferasirox (oral) or Deferoxamine (IV/SC).

cards.q: Quantitative organ assessment method considered the non-invasive gold standard for tracking tissue iron overload?
cards.a: T2* MRI of the liver and heart. Porphyrias and Heme Synthesis Defects

cards.q: Enzyme deficiency responsible for Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP)?
cards.a: Porphobilinogen (PBG) deaminase.

cards.q: Classic clinical presentation pentad of Acute Intermittent Porphyria?
cards.a: Painful abdomen, Polyneuropathy, Psychiatic disturbances, Purple-red urine, and Precipitated by drugs/alcohol.

cards.q: Two primary compounds that accumulate in the urine during an Acute Intermittent Porphyria crisis?
cards.a: ALA (aminolevulinic acid) and PBG (porphobilinogen).

cards.q: Primary therapeutic intervention to abort an acute attack of AIP by suppressing ALA synthase?
cards.a: Intravenous Hemin (or high-dose glucose).

cards.q: Most common porphyria overall, presenting with blistering skin lesions on sun-exposed areas?
cards.a: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda (PCT).

cards.q: Enzyme deficiency responsible for Porphyria Cutanea Tarda?
cards.a: Uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase (UROD).

cards.q: Common chronic infectious disease strongly associated with the development of Porphyria Cutanea Tarda?
cards.a: Hepatitis C virus (HCV). Myeloproliferative and Eosinophilic Variations

cards.q: Mutation strongly associated with Essential Thrombocythemia (ET) and Primary Myelofibrosis outside of JAK2?
cards.a: CALR (calreticulin) or MPL mutation.

cards.q: Platelet count threshold typically used to prompt evaluation for Essential Thrombocythemia?
cards.a: Platelets $>450,000/\mu\text{L}$ sustained on repeat checks.

cards.q: Phenomenon where severe thrombocytosis causes bleeding due to functional loss of high-molecular-weight vWF multimers?
cards.a: Acquired von Willebrand Syndrome.

cards.q: First-line cytoreductive therapy of choice for high-risk Essential Thrombocythemia?
cards.a: Hydroxyurea.

cards.q: Variant of Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia (CMML) requires what absolute monocyte count for diagnosis?
cards.a: Persistent peripheral blood monocytosis $\ge 1,000/\mu\text{L}$.

cards.q: Distinctive genetic fusion product seen in Chronic Eosinophilic Leukemia that responds exceptionally well to Imatinib?
cards.a: FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene. Rare and Complex Lymphoma Entities

cards.q: Rare, highly aggressive Non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma with features intermediate between DLBCL and Burkitt lymphoma?
cards.a: High-grade B-cell lymphoma (often called "double-hit" or "triple-hit" lymphoma if MYC, BCL2, and/or BCL6 are rearranged).

cards.q: T-cell lymphoma subtype characterized by a "necklace" of malignant T-cells around subcutaneous fat cells, mimicking panniculitis?
cards.a: Subcutaneous Panniculitis-like T-cell Lymphoma.

cards.q: Extranodal lymphoma subtype arising in chronic inflammatory states, strongly associated with H. pylori infection in the stomach?
cards.a: MALT lymphoma (Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue lymphoma).

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation frequently driving MALT lymphoma that predicts resistance to H. pylori eradication therapy?
Aggressive extranodal T/NK-cell lymphoma presenting as a destructive midline facial mass, strongly associated with EBV?
cards.a: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type.

cards.q: Rare B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder characteristically localized to the pleural or pericardial cavities in HIV/AIDS patients, driven by HHV-8?
cards.a: Primary Effusion Lymphoma. Complex Coagulation and Thrombophilia Concepts

cards.q: Autosomal dominant condition presenting with telangiectasias, recurrent epistaxis, and arteriovenous malformations (AVMs)?
cards.a: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome).

cards.q: Primary autoantibody target responsible for Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia type II?
cards.a: Platelet Factor 4 (PF4)-heparin complexes.

cards.q: Name of the clinical pre-test probability scoring system used to risk-stratify suspected HIT?
cards.a: The 4Ts Score.

cards.q: Mechanistic explanation for why an isolated Factor XII deficiency prolongs aPTT but does NOT cause clinical bleeding?
cards.a: Factor XII is crucial for in vitro contact activation but redundant for in vivo coagulation initiation.

cards.q: Rare bleeding disorder characterized by normal PT, aPTT, and platelet counts, but presents with delayed wound healing and severe bleeding?
cards.a: Factor XIII deficiency.

cards.q: Definitive laboratory test used to screen for a suspected Factor XIII deficiency?
cards.a: 5M urea clot solubility test (or quantitative Factor XIII activity assay).

cards.q: Mechanism by which Dysfibrinogenemia can present simultaneously with both bleeding and thrombotic risks?
cards.a: Structural fibrinogen mutations alter either its cleavage by thrombin or its ability to bind tissue plasminogen activator (tPA). Transfusion Reactions and Complications (Extended)

cards.q: Expected incremental rise in hemoglobin and platelet count after 1 unit of packed RBCs and 1 unit of apheresis platelets respectively?
cards.a: Hemoglobin rises by $1\text{ g/dL}$; platelet count rises by $30,000\text{ to }50,000/\mu\text{L}$.

cards.q: Transfusion reaction presenting with severe rigors and hyperthermia, caused by bacterial endotoxins contaminating the blood product?
cards.a: Septic transfusion reaction (most common with platelet transfusions due to room temperature storage).

cards.q: Fatal complication of transfusion occurring in immunocompromised hosts where donor T-cells attack recipient tissues?
cards.a: Transfusion-Associated Graft-Versus-Host Disease (TA-GVHD).

cards.q: Standard processing technique used to completely eliminate the risk of Transfusion-Associated Graft-Versus-Host Disease?
cards.a: Gamma or X-ray irradiation of cellular blood products.

cards.q: Phenomenon where severe, life-threatening thrombocytopenia develops 5-10 days after a transfusion due to alloantibodies against human platelet antigen-1a (HPA-1a)?
cards.a: Post-Transfusion Purpura (PTP).

cards.q: Preferred initial management strategy for Post-Transfusion Purpura?
cards.a: Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG) or plasmapheresis. Amyloidosis and Heavy Chain Diseases

cards.q: Protein precursor mismatch driving Primary Systemic Amyloidosis (AL)?
cards.a: Monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains (typically lambda).

cards.q: Characteristic organ biopsy finding when examining systemic amyloid deposits under polarized light microscopy?
cards.a: Apple-green birefringence under Congo red staining.

cards.q: Classic soft-tissue finding in AL amyloidosis characterized by macroglossia and purple periorbital discoloration?
cards.a: "Racoon eyes" (periorbital purpura).

cards.q: Most common protein precursor responsible for Secondary Systemic Amyloidosis (AA)?
cards.a: Serum Amyloid A (an acute-phase reactant driven by chronic inflammation).

cards.q: Plasma cell dyscrasia characterized by the production of truncated heavy chains without attached light chains?
cards.a: Heavy Chain Disease (e.g., Franklin disease, Seligmann disease).

cards.q: Rare systemic disorder presenting with Polyneuropathy, Organomegaly, Endocrinology abnormalities, Monoclonal plasma cell proliferative disorder, and Skin changes?
cards.a: POEMS syndrome. Coagulation Cascade and Lab Interpretations

cards.q: Coagulation factor that initiates the extrinsic pathway of coagulation following vascular injury?
cards.a: Tissue Factor (Factor III).

cards.q: Coagulation factors unique to the intrinsic pathway?
cards.a: Factors XII, XI, IX, and VIII.

cards.q: Coagulation factors comprising the common pathway?
cards.a: Factors X, V, II (prothrombin), and I (fibrinogen).

cards.q: Only coagulation factor that does not circulate as a serine protease zymogen?
cards.a: Factor V (and Factor VIII; they act as cofactors).

cards.q: Coagulation factor responsible for cross-linking fibrin polymers to stabilize a clot?
cards.a: Factor XIII (Fibrin-stabilizing factor).

cards.q: Expected coagulation profile (PT and aPTT) in a patient with a severe Vitamin K deficiency?
cards.a: Both PT and aPTT are prolonged (PT typically prolongs first due to short half-life of Factor VII).

cards.q: Exact mechanism by which Warfarin acts as an anticoagulant?
cards.a: Inhibits Vitamin K Epoxide Reductase Complex 1 (VKORC1), preventing gamma-carboxylation of Factors II, VII, IX, X, and Proteins C/S.

cards.q: Mechanistic reason why Unfractionated Heparin prolongs aPTT more significantly than Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin (LMWH)?
cards.a: Unfractionated heparin binds antithrombin to inhibit both Thrombin and Factor Xa, whereas LMWH principally inhibits Factor Xa.

cards.q: Laboratory assay used to accurately monitor therapeutic levels of Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin when clinically indicated?
cards.a: Anti-Factor Xa assay. Myelodysplastic/Myeloproliferative Overlap and Rare Anemias

cards.q: Distinctive bone marrow feature that distinguishes Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia (CMML) from CML?
cards.a: Absence of the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene and presence of persistent peripheral monocytosis.

cards.q: Diagnostic genetic deletion confirming Secondary Acute Myeloid Leukemia arising from prior MDS or chemotherapy?
cards.a: Deletion of chromosome 5 (del(5q)) or chromosome 7 (del(7q)).

cards.q: Rare congenital normocytic anemia presenting with triphalangeal thumbs and a striking increased risk of osteosarcoma and AML?
cards.a: Diamond-Blackfan Anemia.

cards.q: Autosomal recessive disorder presenting with progressive pancytopenia, café-au-lait spots, microcephaly, and a high risk of squamous cell carcinomas?
cards.a: Fanconi Anemia.

cards.q: Mechanistic cause of anemia in Lead Poisoning outside of enzyme inhibition?
cards.a: Inhibition of pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase, causing ribosomal RNA degradation failure and subsequent basophilic stippling.

cards.q: Classic clinical triad of Plummer-Vinson Syndrome?
cards.a: Iron deficiency anemia, esophageal webs, and dysphagia. Lymphoma and Leukemia Molecular Pathogenesis

cards.q: Immunophenotypic cell surface marker used to definitively identify classic Hodgkin Lymphoma Reed-Sternberg cells via immunohistochemistry?
cards.a: CD15 and CD30 positive (CD45 negative).

cards.q: Histological variant of Hodgkin Lymphoma characterized by "popcorn cells" that express B-cell markers like CD20?
cards.a: Nodular Lymphocyte Predominant Hodgkin Lymphoma (NLPHL).

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation and gene rearrangement characteristic of Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma (ALCL)?
cards.a: $\text{t}(2;5)$ resulting in the NPM-ALK fusion gene.

cards.q: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma subtype characterized by primary involvement of the skin, presenting as generalized erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, and atypical T-cells with cerebriform nuclei?
cards.a: Sézary Syndrome (leukemic phase of Mycosis Fungoides).

cards.q: Unique oncogenic mechanism driving Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) in up to $30\%$ of cases?
cards.a: BCL6 gene rearrangements or dysregulation on chromosome 3q27.

cards.q: Primary viral driver implicated in Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma in immunocompromised/HIV patients?
cards.a: Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV).

cards.q: Translocation associated with a subset of Acute Myeloid Leukemias that carries a highly favorable prognosis?
cards.a: $\text{t}(8;21)$ involving the RUNX1-RUNX1T1 fusion.

cards.q: Cytogenetic abnormality in AML involving chromosome 16 that correlates with abnormal eosinophils in the bone marrow and a favorable prognosis?
cards.a: $\text{inv}(16)$ or $\text{t}(16;16)$. Non-Malignant Hematological Emergencies

cards.q: First line medical therapy for acute, severe bleeding in a patient taking direct oral Factor Xa inhibitors?
cards.a: Andexanet alfa.

cards.q: Immediate management step for a sickle cell patient presenting with sudden-onset severe dyspnea, new chest infiltrate, and hypoxia?
cards.a: Emergent empiric antibiotics, supplemental oxygen, IV fluids, and consideration for exchange transfusion (Acute Chest Syndrome).

cards.q: Pathophysiological driver of priapism in male pediatric patients with Sickle Cell Disease?
cards.a: Vaso-occlusion and stasis of sickled erythrocytes within the corpora cavernosa.

cards.q: Vital intervention required immediately for a neutropenic cancer patient presenting with a single oral temperature reading of $\ge 38.3^\circ\text{C}$ ($101^\circ\text{F}$)?
cards.a: Draw blood cultures and immediately administer empiric broad-spectrum antipseudomonal IV antibiotics (e.g., Cefepime).

cards.q: Major electrolyte abnormality that can precipitate life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias during massive blood transfusion protocols?
cards.a: Hypocalcemia (caused by citrate preservative binding free calcium). Histiocytic and Dendritic Cell Disorders

cards.q: Clonal proliferation of dendritic antigen-presenting cells presenting with lytic bone lesions, skin rashes, and diabetes insipidus?
cards.a: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis (LCH).

cards.q: Pathognomonic electron microscopy finding in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis?
cards.a: Birbeck granules (tennis-racket shaped structures).

cards.q: Key immunohistochemical markers used to confirm Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis?
cards.a: CD1a and Langerin (CD207) positivity.

cards.q: Highly aggressive, life-threatening syndrome characterized by cytopenias, hepatosplenomegaly, and hyperferritinemia due to overactivation of macrophages?
cards.a: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH).

cards.q: Diagnostic ferritin threshold typically used as a major criterion for Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis?
cards.a: Serum ferritin $\ge 500\text{ }\mu\text{g/L}$ (often $>3,000\text{ }\mu\text{g/L}$ is highly suggestive).

cards.q: Common genetic mutations identified in adult presentations of Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis?
cards.a: BRAF V600E mutation (found in roughly $50\%$ of cases). Advanced Hypercoagulable and Thrombotic Concepts

cards.q: Autosomal dominant condition presenting with recurrent venous thromboembolisms where standard therapeutic doses of Heparin fail to prolong the aPTT?
cards.a: Antithrombin (ATIII) deficiency.

cards.q: Specific clinical scenario where an Antiphospholipid Syndrome patient requires lifelong therapeutic anticoagulation with Warfarin over DOACs?
cards.a: Triple-positive Antiphospholipid Syndrome (positive for Lupus Anticoagulant, Anticardiolipin, and Anti-beta2-glycoprotein I).

cards.q: Rare condition presenting with a combination of arterial/venous thromboses, livedo reticularis, and recurrent ischemic strokes in young adults?
cards.a: Sneddon Syndrome.

cards.q: Mechanistic cause of neonatal purpura fulminans immediately after birth?
cards.a: Homozygous Protein C or Protein S deficiency.

cards.q: Coagulation test modification required to confirm the presence of a Lupus Anticoagulant?
cards.a: Demonstration of phospholipid-dependence using the Dilute Russell's Viper Venom Time (dRVVT) or high-phospholipid neutralization.

cards.q: Most common site of visceral vein thrombosis in patients diagnosed with Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH)?
cards.a: Hepatic vein thrombosis (Budd-Chiari syndrome). Bone Marrow Microenvironment and Specialized Anemias

cards.q: Key stromal-derived cytokine essential for the survival, proliferation, and differentiation of early hematopoietic stem cells?
cards.a: Stem Cell Factor (SCF) (or c-Kit ligand).

cards.q: Specialized macrophage-containing structures in the bone marrow where erythroblast maturation occurs?
cards.a: Erythroblastic islands.

cards.q: Autosomal dominant pure red cell aplasia linked to ribosomal protein gene mutations ($RPS19$)?
cards.a: Diamond-Blackfan Anemia.

cards.q: Distinctive physical exam sign on the hands that differentiates Diamond-Blackfan Anemia from Fanconi Anemia?
cards.a: Triphalangeal thumbs in Diamond-Blackfan; absent or hypoplastic thumbs/radii in Fanconi.

cards.q: Acquired pure red cell aplasia (PRCA) is classically associated with what encapsulated mediastinal tumor?
cards.a: Thymoma.

cards.q: Rare, inherited normocytic anemia characterized by multinucleated erythroblasts and a positive acidified serum lysis (Ham) test?
cards.a: Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemia (CDA). Hemoglobinopathies: Structural Variants and Genetics

cards.q: Structural hemoglobin variant that causes Hemoglobin C disease?
cards.a: Lysine substitution for glutamic acid at position 6 of the beta-globin chain.

cards.q: Classic morphology of erythrocytes on a peripheral blood smear from a patient with Hemoglobin CC disease?
cards.a: HbC crystals (rod-shaped/rectangular structures) and target cells.

cards.q: Structural variant where glutamic acid is replaced by lysine at position 26 of the beta-globin chain, common in Southeast Asia?
cards.a: Hemoglobin E ($HbE$).

cards.q: Underlying genetic mechanism responsible for the vast majority of Alpha-Thalassemia cases?
cards.a: Gene deletions (large structural deletions via unequal crossing over).

cards.q: Underlying genetic mechanism responsible for the vast majority of Beta-Thalassemia cases?
cards.a: Point mutations (splicing, promoter, or nonsense mutations).

cards.q: Hemoglobin variant formed by two alpha chains and two delta chains ($\alpha_2\delta_2$)?
cards.a: Hemoglobin $A_2$ ($HbA_2$).

cards.q: Definitive quantitative assay used to precisely monitor Hemoglobin S levels in sickle cell patients undergoing exchange transfusion?
cards.a: High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC). Immune and Non-Immune Hemolytic Pathophysiology

cards.q: Specific complement regulatory protein missing in PNH that normally degrades C3 convertases?
cards.a: CD55 (Decay-accelerating factor / DAF).

cards.q: Specific complement regulatory protein missing in PNH that normally prevents assembly of the Membrane Attack Complex (MAC)?
cards.a: CD59 (Membrane inhibitor of reactive lysis / MIRL).

cards.q: Humanized monoclonal antibody targeting complement component C5 used to treat Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria?
cards.a: Eculizumab (or Ravulizumab).

cards.q: Classic mechanism of cell destruction in Microangiopathic Hemolytic Anemia (MAHA)?
cards.a: Mechanical shearing of erythrocytes as they pass through fibrin-platelet meshworks in microvessels.

cards.q: Physical footprint of intravascular hemolysis measured via a decrease in which specific serum transport protein?
cards.a: Haptoglobin.

cards.q: Oxidation product of hemoglobin breakdown that accumulates in the urine during sustained, severe intravascular hemolysis?
cards.a: Hemosiderin (Hemosiderinuria).

cards.q: Protozoal intraerythrocytic infection that mimics G6PD deficiency by inducing hemolytic anemia and forming "Maltese cross" tetrads?
cards.a: Babesiosis. Advanced Leukemia Classification and Cytogenetics

cards.q: Cell surface markers used to differentiate early T-cell ALL from B-cell ALL via flow cytometry?
cards.a: T-ALL expresses CD3, CD7, and CD2; B-ALL expresses CD19, CD10, and CD22.

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation $\text{t}(12;21)$ involving $ETV6-RUNX1$ confers what type of prognosis in pediatric B-ALL?
cards.a: Highly favorable prognosis.

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation $\text{t}(1;19)$ involving $TCF3-PBX1$ confers what type of prognosis in pediatric B-ALL?
cards.a: Unfavorable/poor prognosis.

cards.q: Specific WHO classification cytogenetic rearrangement in AML that involves the $RUNX1-RUNX1T1$ fusion?
Cytogenetic abnormality in AML that results in the $CBFB-MYH11$ fusion protein?
The presence of NPM1 or CEBPA mutations in the absence of FLT3-ITD mutations in AML signals what prognosis?
cards.a: Favorable prognosis (in cytogenetically normal AML).

cards.q: Cell-of-origin classification marker that identifies the chronic phase of CML from leukemoid reactions?
cards.a: Low or zero Leukocyte Alkaline Phosphatase (LAP) score in CML.

cards.q: Splenic pathology classic for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia?
cards.a: Massive splenomegaly due to extensive extramedullary hematopoiesis in the red pulp. Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma and T-Cell Malignancies

cards.q: Cell of origin for Follicular Lymphoma?
cards.a: Germinal center B-cells.

cards.q: Cell surface marker universally absent on normal B-cells but characteristically aberrant/positive on Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) B-cells?
cards.a: CD5.

cards.q: Pathognomonic tissue biopsy layout defining Mantle Cell Lymphoma?
cards.a: Monomorphic expansion of small-to-medium lymphocytes surrounding germinal centers in the mantle zone.

cards.q: Unique biological mechanism behind the growth of Gastric MALT lymphoma?
cards.a: $H.\text{ pylori}$-specific T-cells stimulate the malignant B-cell clone via cytokine signaling.

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation $\text{t}(11;18)$ in MALT lymphoma fuses which two genes?
cards.a: $API2$ and $MALT1$.

cards.q: Most common clinical presentation of Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma (ALCL) in young adults?
cards.a: Lymphadenopathy with skin/soft tissue involvement and systemic B symptoms.

cards.q: Hallmark cell morphology describing Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma?
cards.a: Large "hallmark" cells with kidney- or horseshoe-shaped nuclei and a prominent perinuclear halo.

cards.q: Target antigen for the antibody-drug conjugate Brentuximab Vedotin used in Hodgkin Lymphoma and ALCL?
cards.a: CD30. Complex Hypercoagulability and Endothelial Pathology

cards.q: Autoimmune clotting disorder presenting with prolonged aPTT, livedo reticularis, and false-positive VDRL/RPR tests for syphilis?
cards.a: Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS).

cards.q: Primary mechanism by which anti-beta2-glycoprotein I antibodies promote a prothrombotic state?
cards.a: Activation of endothelial cells, platelets, and monocytes, upregulating tissue factor expression.

cards.q: Inherited condition caused by a mutation in the prothrombin gene untranslated region that increases prothrombin mRNA stability?
cards.a: Prothrombin G20210A mutation.

cards.q: Most accurate timing to check Protein C or Protein S functional activity levels to evaluate for inherited deficiency?
cards.a: At least 2 weeks after terminating oral Warfarin therapy and when the patient is free from acute thrombosis.

cards.q: Rare, life-threatening complication of Unfractionated Heparin infusion presenting with a $>50\%$ drop in platelets within 5-10 days?
cards.a: Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) Type II.

cards.q: Specific functional diagnostic confirmation test for HIT Type II that measures radioactive isotope emission?
cards.a: Serotonin Release Assay (SRA). Platelet Function Defects and Vascular Purpuras

cards.q: Inherited qualitative platelet disorder due to a deficiency in the Glycoprotein Ib-IX-V complex?
cards.a: Bernard-Soulier Syndrome.

cards.q: Inherited qualitative platelet disorder due to a deficiency in the Glycoprotein IIb/IIIa complex?
cards.a: Glanzmann Thrombasthenia.

cards.q: Unique laboratory feature that differentiates Bernard-Soulier Syndrome from Glanzmann Thrombasthenia on a peripheral blood smear?
cards.a: Presence of giant platelets in Bernard-Soulier Syndrome.

cards.q: Effect of adding normal plasma to a platelet agglutination test using Ristocetin in a patient with Bernard-Soulier Syndrome?
cards.a: No correction (because the defect is in the structural platelet GP Ib receptor, not a plasma factor).

cards.q: Effect of adding normal plasma to a platelet agglutination test using Ristocetin in a patient with von Willebrand Disease?
cards.a: Correction (because normal plasma replenishes the missing von Willebrand Factor).

cards.q: Acquired vascular purpura caused by Vitamin C deficiency affecting collagen cross-linking?
cards.a: Scurvy.

cards.q: Classic perifollicular skin findings pathognomonic for severe Vitamin C deficiency?
cards.a: Perifollicular hemorrhages and "corkscrew" hairs. Myelofibrosis and Secondary Myeloproliferative States

cards.q: Principal bone marrow cytokine responsible for driving the extensive reactive collagen fibrosis in Primary Myelofibrosis?
cards.a: Transforming Growth Factor-beta (TGF-$\beta$) (released from clonal megakaryocytes).

cards.q: Name given to the dry tap bone marrow aspiration attempt classic in Primary Myelofibrosis and Hairy Cell Leukemia?
cards.a: Punctio sicca.

cards.q: Most common physiological cause of a secondary polycythemia presenting with elevated erythropoietin (EPO) levels?
cards.a: Chronic hypoxemia (e.g., severe COPD, sleep apnea, high altitude) or EPO-secreting tumors.

cards.q: Paraneoplastic syndrome condition where a renal cell carcinoma or cerebellar hemangioblastoma causes erythrocytosis?
cards.a: Inappropriate secondary polycythemia (via autonomous EPO production).

cards.q: Pathophysiological driver of erythromelalgia (burning pain and erythema in extremities) in Essential Thrombocythemia?
cards.a: Platelet microvascular occlusion and subsequent endothelial inflammation. Special Storage Profiles and Plasma Cell Variants

cards.q: Diagnostic plasma cell threshold required to classify a patient as Smoldering Multiple Myeloma?
cards.a: Serum M-protein $\ge 3\text{ g/dL}$ OR bone marrow clonal plasma cells $10\%\text{ to }60\%$ without CRAB features.

cards.q: Cytogenetic deletion strongly associated with high-risk Multiple Myeloma and short survival times?
cards.a: Deletion $17\text{p}$ ($del(17p)$ losing the p53 gene).

cards.q: Primary mode of therapeutic action for Immunomodulatory drugs (IMiDs like Lenalidomide) in Multiple Myeloma?
cards.a: Binding to Cereblon, leading to the selective degradation of Ikaros and Aiolos transcription factors.

cards.q: Mechanism of action for Bortezomib in the treatment of Multiple Myeloma?
cards.a: Reversible inhibition of the $26\text{S}$ proteasome, inducing unfolded protein stress and apoptosis.

cards.q: Specific organ dysfunction that makes the usage of systemic Bisphosphonates highly risky or contraindicated in Myeloma patients?
cards.a: Severe Renal Insufficiency ($\text{GFR} < 30\text{ mL/min}$).

cards.q: Diagnostic criteria for Light Chain Smoldering Multiple Myeloma?
cards.a: Involved/uninvolved serum free light chain ratio $\ge 100$ plus bone marrow plasma cells $<60\%$. Coagulation Cascade Regulation and Thrombophilia Pathology

cards.q: Endothelial cell surface receptor that binds Thrombin to activate the Protein C pathway?
cards.a: Thrombomodulin.

cards.q: Co-factor that accelerates the inactivation of Factors Va and VIIIa by Activated Protein C?
cards.a: Protein S.

cards.q: Plasma inhibitor that directly neutralizes Tissue Factor-Factor VIIa-Factor Xa complexes?
cards.a: Tissue Factor Pathway Inhibitor (TFPI).

cards.q: Specific mechanism by which Antithrombin III neutralizes Thrombin and Factor Xa?
cards.a: Functions as a suicide substrate protease inhibitor, forming a stable 1:1 complex with the active site of the clotting factors.

cards.q: Specific structural component of the endothelial surface that naturally accelerates Antithrombin III activity?
cards.a: Heparan sulfate proteoglycans.

cards.q: Diagnostic pitfall when testing for Antithrombin III deficiency during an acute thrombotic event?
cards.a: Acute thrombosis can transiently consume Antithrombin III, leading to a false-positive diagnosis.

cards.q: Minimum duration a patient must be off oral Warfarin before testing for functional Protein C and S levels?
cards.a: Two weeks. Hemolytic Anemias: Enzymatic and Membrane Details

cards.q: Metabolic pathway in which Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase (G6PD) operates to protect RBCs from oxidative stress?
cards.a: Hexose monophosphate (HMP) shunt.

cards.q: Key reducing equivalent generated by G6PD that maintains glutathione in its active state?
cards.a: NADPH.

cards.q: Molecular consequence to hemoglobin when NADPH is depleted under oxidative stress?
cards.a: Sulfhydryl groups on Hb cross-link, causing the protein to denature and precipitate as Heinz bodies.

cards.q: Specific physiological mechanism by which "bite cells" are formed in G6PD deficiency?
cards.a: Splenic macrophages pluck out denatured hemoglobin inclusions (Heinz bodies) from the erythrocytes.

cards.q: Diagnostic pitfall when testing G6PD enzyme activity levels immediately after an acute hemolytic crisis?
cards.a: False-negative result due to the destruction of older, enzyme-deficient RBCs and a high concentration of young, enzyme-replete reticulocytes.

cards.q: Transmembrane transport protein mutated in the majority of patients with autosomal dominant Hereditary Spherocytosis?
cards.a: Ankyrin (encoded by the ANK1 gene).

cards.q: Primary site of RBC destruction in Hereditary Spherocytosis?
cards.a: The splenic cords of Billroth (extravascular hemolysis). Hemoglobinopathies and Quantitative Globin Defects

cards.q: Normal physiological composition of adult Hemoglobin A ($HbA$)?
cards.a: Two alpha-globin chains and two beta-globin chains ($\alpha_2\beta_2$).

cards.q: Normal physiological composition of fetal Hemoglobin F ($HbF$)?
cards.a: Two alpha-globin chains and two gamma-globin chains ($\alpha_2\gamma_2$).

cards.q: Exact amino acid substitution at position 6 of the beta-chain that results in Hemoglobin S ($HbS$)?
cards.a: Substitution of hydrophilic glutamic acid with hydrophobic valine.

cards.q: Molecular consequence when deoxygenated Hemoglobin S molecules aggregate?
cards.a: Hydrophobic interactions cause polymerization into long, rigid crystalline polymers that distort the RBC into a sickle shape.

cards.q: Exact amino acid substitution at position 6 of the beta-chain that results in Hemoglobin C ($HbC$)?
cards.a: Substitution of glutamic acid with lysine.

cards.q: Microscopic structural morphology typical of Hemoglobin C crystals seen in homozygous HbCC patients?
cards.a: Hexagonal, dark-staining, rod-like intracellular crystals.

cards.q: Pathophysiological mechanism behind the development of Beta-Thalassemia major?
cards.a: Severe reduction or complete absence of beta-globin synthesis leading to an excess of unpaired, unstable alpha-globin chains that precipitate and cause ineffective erythropoiesis. Acute Leukemia Cytogenetics and Molecular Drivers

cards.q: Cytogenetic translocation $\text{t}(15;17)(\text{q}24;\text{q}21)$ fuses which two genes?
cards.a: PML (promyelocytic leukemia) and RARA (retinoic acid receptor alpha).

cards.q: Biological function disrupted by the PML-RARA fusion protein in Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia?
cards.a: Blocks myeloid differentiation at the promyelocytic stage by recruiting histone deacetylases to repress transcription.

cards.q: Cytogenetic translocation $\text{t}(8;21)(\text{q}22;\text{q}22)$ in AML fuses which two genes?
cards.a: RUNX1 (AML1) and RUNX1T1 (ETO).

cards.q: Cytogenetic inversion $\text{inv}(16)(\text{p}13.1\text{q}22)$ in Acute Myeloid Leukemia fuses which two genes?
cards.a: CBFB (core-binding factor subunit beta) and MYH11.

cards.q: Prognostic significance of $\text{t}(8;21)$ or $\text{inv}(16)$ in a patient with de novo Acute Myeloid Leukemia?
cards.a: Confers a favorable prognosis (classified as Core Binding Factor AML).

cards.q: Internal tandem duplication mutation in which gene confers a poor prognosis in cytogenetically normal AML?
cards.a: FLT3 (Fms-like tyrosine kinase 3).

cards.q: Cell surface protein configuration that characterizes the immunophenotype of standard Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia lymphoblasts?
cards.a: TdT positive, CD19 positive, and CD10 positive (Common ALL Antigen / CALLA). Chronic Lymphoproliferative and Plasma Cell Disorders

cards.q: Clonal cell surface marker expression pattern that definitively differentiates CLL from Mantle Cell Lymphoma via flow cytometry?
cards.a: Both express CD5, but CLL is CD23 positive and Mantle Cell Lymphoma is CD23 negative.

cards.q: Histological pattern within lymph nodes when CLL manifests primarily as a solid tumor (Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma)?
cards.a: Diffuse effacement of nodal architecture with proliferation centers containing prolymphocytes and paraimmunoblasts.

cards.q: Laboratory parameter used in the Rai Staging System to classify Stage IV Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia?
cards.a: Thrombocytopenia (platelets $<100,000/\mu\text{L}$).

cards.q: Diagnostic evaluation required to differentiate Smoldering Multiple Myeloma from Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance (MGUS)?
cards.a: Quantifying clonal bone marrow plasma cells ($10\text{ to }60\%$ in Smoldering vs. $<10\%$ in MGUS).

cards.q: Most common light-chain configuration found in systemic AL amyloidosis secondary to plasma cell dyscrasias?
cards.a: Lambda ($\lambda$) light chains.

cards.q: Mechanism by which Multiple Myeloma plasma cells induce lytic bone lesions?
cards.a: Secretion of RANKL and DKK1, which activates osteoclasts and suppresses osteoblasts. Chronic Myeloproliferative Neoplasms

cards.q: Translocation $\text{t}(9;22)(\text{q}34.1;\text{q}11.2)$ relocates the c-ABL proto-oncogene to which specific gene site on chromosome 22?
cards.a: BCR (breakpoint cluster region).

cards.q: Intracellular signaling pathways constitutively activated by the BCR-ABL1 fusion tyrosine kinase?
cards.a: JAK/STAT, RAS/MAPK, and PI3K/AKT pathways.

cards.q: Specific JAK2 mutation found in nearly all cases of Polycythemia Vera?
cards.a: A valine-to-phenylalanine substitution at codon 617 (JAK2 V617F) in the pseudokinase domain.

cards.q: Pathophysiological effect of the JAK2 V617F mutation on hematopoietic growth factor receptors?
cards.a: Confers hypersensitivity to erythropoietin, thrombopoietin, and G-CSF, allowing cytokine-independent signaling.

cards.q: Major bone marrow biopsy feature that distinguishes Essential Thrombocythemia from Primary Myelofibrosis in early stages?
cards.a: ET shows loose clusters of giant, mature megakaryocytes without significant reticulin fibrosis.

cards.q: Serum erythropoietin (EPO) level expected in a patient with Polycythemia Vera vs. Secondary Polycythemia?
cards.a: Suppressed/low in Polycythemia Vera; elevated in Secondary Polycythemia. Advanced Coagulopathies and Platelet Dysfunctions

cards.q: Target antigen of the autoantibodies driving Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP)?
cards.a: Platelet membrane glycoproteins GPIIb/IIIa or GPIb/IX.

cards.q: Plasma metalloprotease responsible for cleaving ultra-large von Willebrand factor (vWF) multimers?
cards.a: ADAMTS13.

cards.q: Pathophysiological mechanism behind the microvascular thrombosis in Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP)?
cards.a: Accumulation of uncleaved ultra-large vWF multimers causes spontaneous platelet aggregation and microvascular shear stress.

cards.q: Crucial laboratory parameter that differentiates TTP/HUS from Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)?
cards.a: Coagulation profiles (PT and aPTT) are normal in TTP/HUS but prolonged in DIC.

cards.q: Inherited structural defect responsible for Bernard-Soulier Syndrome?
cards.a: Deficiency or dysfunction of the GPIb-IX-V receptor complex on the platelet membrane.

cards.q: Inherited structural defect responsible for Glanzmann Thrombasthenia?
cards.a: Deficiency or dysfunction of the GPIIb/IIIa (integrin $\alpha_{\text{IIb}}\beta_3$) receptor complex on the platelet membrane.

cards.q: Laboratory aggregation pattern diagnostic for von Willebrand Disease when evaluating platelet-rich plasma?
cards.a: Impaired platelet agglutination to Ristocetin, which normalizes upon the addition of normal plasma. Lymphoma Pathogenesis and Immunophenotypical Nuances

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation t(8;14)(q24;q32) characteristically moves which proto-oncogene to the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus?
cards.a: MYC.

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation t(14;18)(q32;q21) characteristically fuses the BCL2 gene to which locus?
cards.a: Immunoglobulin heavy chain (IGH) locus.

cards.q: Molecular mechanism by which BCL2 overexpression promotes cell survival in Follicular Lymphoma?
cards.a: It stabilizes the outer mitochondrial membrane, preventing the release of cytochrome c and inhibiting apoptosis.

cards.q: Chromosomal translocation t(11;14)(q13;q32) overexpresses which protein?
cards.a: Cyclin D1 (encoded by the CCND1 gene).

cards.q: Primary physiological function of Cyclin D1 that is dysregulated in Mantle Cell Lymphoma?
cards.a: Promotes transition from G1 to S phase of the cell cycle by phosphorylating and inactivating the Retinoblastoma (Rb) protein.

cards.q: Specific translocation t(11;18)(q21;q21) seen in gastric MALT lymphoma fuses which two genes?
cards.a: BIRC3 (API2) and MALT1.

cards.q: Immunophenotypic profile that characterizes classic Reed-Sternberg cells?
cards.a: CD15 positive, CD30 positive, and CD45 negative.

cards.q: Immunophenotypic profile that distinguishes Nodular Lymphocyte Predominant Hodgkin Lymphoma (NLPHL) from classic Hodgkin Lymphoma?
cards.a: Popcorn cells in NLPHL are CD20 positive, CD45 positive, CD15 negative, and CD30 negative. Porphyrias and Disorders of Heme Biosynthesis

cards.q: Enzyme deficiency responsible for the clinical presentation of Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP)?
cards.a: Porphobilinogen deaminase (also known as hydroxymethylbilane synthase).

cards.q: Major neurotoxic precursors that accumulate in plasma and urine during an acute flare of AIP?
cards.a: Aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG).

cards.q: Primary enzymatic step inhibited by lead poisoning in the heme synthesis pathway?
cards.a: Aminolevulinic acid dehydratase (ALA dehydratase) and ferrochelatase.

cards.q: Intermediate product that accumulates in erythrocytes as a direct consequence of lead poisoning?
cards.a: Zinc protoporphyrin.

cards.q: Enzyme deficiency responsible for Porphyria Cutanea Tarda (PCT)?
cards.a: Uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase.

cards.q: Classic skin pathology seen on sun-exposed areas of patients with Porphyria Cutanea Tarda?
cards.a: Subepidermal blistering, fragility, and hyperpigmentation due to porphyrin activation by UV light.

cards.q: First-line medical therapies used to downregulate heme synthesis during an acute attack of AIP?
cards.a: Intravenous hemin or high-dose glucose infusions (which repress hepatic ALA synthase-1). Bone Marrow Failure and Myelodysplastic Pathology

cards.q: Pathognomonic bone marrow erythroid finding in myelodysplastic syndrome characterized by a ring of iron granules around the nucleus?
cards.a: Ring sideroblast.

cards.q: Exact organelle where iron accumulates abnormally to form the morphology of a ring sideroblast?
cards.a: Mitochondria.

cards.q: Genetic mutation strongly associated with the presence of ring sideroblasts in Myelodysplastic Syndrome?
cards.a: SF3B1 mutation (a spliceosome gene).

cards.q: Nuclear morphology change in neutrophils ("pseudo-Pelger-Huët anomaly") classic for Myelodysplastic Syndrome?
cards.a: Hyposegmented (bilobed or monolobed) neutrophilic nuclei.

cards.q: Chromosomal deletion associated with a specific myelodysplastic syndrome variant that responds dramatically to lenalidomide?
cards.a: Isolated deletion of the long arm of chromosome 5 (del(5q)).

cards.q: Molecular defect driving Fanconi Anemia?
cards.a: Defect in the multiprotein FANCA-complex responsible for DNA interstrand cross-link repair.

cards.q: Classic developmental phenotype that distinguishes Diamond-Blackfan Anemia from Fanconi Anemia?
cards.a: Diamond-Blackfan shows pure red cell aplasia and triphalangeal thumbs; Fanconi shows pancytopenia and absent or hypoplastic thumbs. Specialized Hypercoagulable Conditions

cards.q: Structural alteration caused by the Factor V Leiden mutation?
cards.a: A single point mutation (Arg506Gln) at the cleavage site of Factor V.

cards.q: Functional consequence of the Arg506Gln mutation in Factor V Leiden?
cards.a: Renders Factor Va resistant to cleavage and inactivation by Activated Protein C (APC).

cards.q: Molecular basis of the Prothrombin G20210A mutation?
cards.a: A point mutation in the 3' untranslated region of the prothrombin gene that increases mRNA stability and prothrombin expression.

cards.q: Mechanism of hypercoagulability in a patient with an Antithrombin III deficiency?
cards.a: Failure to neutralize serine protease clotting factors (Thrombin, Factor Xa, Factor IXa).

cards.q: Mechanistic reason why initiating Warfarin therapy can induce temporary hypercoagulability?
cards.a: Warfarin depletes Protein C and Protein S (short half-lives) faster than it depletes clotting factors II, IX, and X.

cards.q: Diagnostic test used to confirm a Lupus Anticoagulant that utilizes viper venom?
cards.a: Dilute Russell's Viper Venom Time (dRVVT).

cards.q: True underlying pathophysiology behind the false-positive VDRL/RPR test in Antiphospholipid Syndrome?
cards.a: Antibodies cross-react with the cardiolipin antigen used in the syphilis screening assay. Transfusion Complications and Precision Management

cards.q: Transfusion reaction presenting with fever, chills, and mild dyspnea within 1 to 6 hours, driven by pre-formed cytokines in the blood product bag?
cards.a: Febrile Non-Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction.

cards.q: Processing step utilized by blood banks to drastically reduce the incidence of Febrile Non-Hemolytic Transfusion Reactions?
cards.a: Leukoreduction (filtering out donor white blood cells prior to storage).

cards.q: Transfusion reaction presenting as acute hypoxemia and non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema within 6 hours of a transfusion?
cards.a: Transfusion-Related Acute Lung Injury (TRALI).

cards.q: Primary immunological driver behind Transfusion-Related Acute Lung Injury (TRALI)?
cards.a: Donor HLA or neutrophil-specific antibodies targeting and activating recipient neutrophils within the pulmonary vasculature.

cards.q: Clinical feature that distinguishes Transfusion-Associated Circulatory Overload (TACO) from TRALI?
cards.a: TACO presents with signs of volume overload, such as hypertension, elevated JVP, and response to diuretics.

cards.q: Storage requirement used to prevent Transfusion-Associated Graft-Versus-Host Disease (TA-GVHD) in immunocompromised recipients?
cards.a: Gamma or X-ray irradiation of cellular blood products to inactivate donor T-lymphocytes.

cards.q: Phenomenon where profound thrombocytopenia occurs 5 to 10 days post-transfusion due to alloantibodies against human platelet antigens?
cards.a: Post-Transfusion Purpura (PTP). Histiocytic and Histological Borderlands

cards.q: Clonal neoplastic proliferation of dendritic cells presenting with lytic bone lesions, skin rash, and diabetes insipidus?
cards.a: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis (LCH).

cards.q: Pathognomonic electron microscopy finding inside Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis cells?
cards.a: Birbeck granules (tennis-racket shaped cytoplasmic structures).

cards.q: Immunohistochemical cell surface markers positive in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis?
cards.a: CD1a and Langerin (CD207).

cards.q: Aggressive, life-threatening syndrome characterized by cytopenias, massive hepatosplenomegaly, and hyperferritinemia driven by uninhibited macrophage activation?
cards.a: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH).

cards.q: Principal cytokine that drives the hyperactivation of macrophages and subsequent hemophagocytosis in HLH?
cards.a: Interferon-gamma (IFN-γ).

cards.q: Histological pattern in lymph nodes showing an expansion of marginal zone B-cells that form a halo around reactive germinal centers?
cards.a: Marginal Zone Lymphoma.

cards.q: Rare plasma cell variant disorder presenting with polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal protein, and skin changes?
cards.a: POEMS syndrome. Direct Oral Anticoagulants (DOACs) and Specific Reversal Agents

cards.q: Specific mechanism of action of Dabigatran?
cards.a: Direct, competitive thrombin (Factor IIa) inhibitor.

cards.q: Specific mechanism of action of Rivaroxaban, Apixaban, and Edoxaban?
cards.a: Direct, selective inhibitors of free and clot-bound Factor Xa.

cards.q: Monoclonal antibody fragment used for the immediate reversal of Dabigatran?
cards.a: Idarucizumab.

cards.q: Decoy receptor protein used to reverse direct Factor Xa inhibitors (Rivaroxaban and Apixaban)?
cards.a: Andexanet alfa.

cards.q: Standard coagulation screening test most prolonged by therapeutic doses of Dabigatran?
cards.a: Thrombin Time (TT) (and aPTT).

cards.q: Primary route of elimination for Dabigatran that requires strict dosage adjustments in renal failure?
cards.a: Renal clearance ($80\%$). Secondary and Microangiopathic Thrombocytopenias

cards.q: Classic drug-induced thrombocytopenia mechanism associated with Quinine, Sulfa drugs, or Gold salts?
cards.a: Drug-dependent antibodies bind to platelet glycoproteins only in the presence of the drug, causing accelerated clearance.

cards.q: Pathophysiological mechanism behind Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) Type I?
cards.a: Direct non-immunologic pro-aggregatory effect of heparin on platelets, occurring within 1–2 days and presenting with mild, transient thrombocytopenia.

cards.q: Minimum percentage drop in platelet count from baseline that defines a positive "4Ts" criteria component for HIT Type II?
cards.a: $>50\%$ drop in platelet count.

cards.q: Timing window post-heparin exposure during which HIT Type II characteristically manifests?
cards.a: 5 to 10 days (or within 24 hours if pre-exposed to heparin in the past 100 days).

cards.q: Standard non-heparin anticoagulant of choice for a patient with confirmed HIT who has concurrent severe hepatic impairment?
cards.a: Bivalirudin or Fondaparinux (Argatroban is avoided/dose-reduced due to hepatic metabolism).

cards.q: Pathophysiological driver of diarrhea-associated (typical) Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS)?
cards.a: Shiga toxin localizes to the renal endothelial cells, causing endothelial damage, microthrombi formation, and mechanical hemolysis.

cards.q: Alternative (atypical) Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (aHUS) is primarily driven by genetic mutations in what physiological pathway?
cards.a: Regulatory proteins of the alternative complement pathway (e.g., Factor H, Factor I, or CD46).

cards.q: Humanized monoclonal antibody targeting complement protein C5 used as first-line therapy for atypical HUS?
cards.a: Eculizumab. Platelet Storage Pool and Adhesion Defects

cards.q: Specific substance stored inside platelet alpha-granules that is deficient in Gray Platelet Syndrome?
cards.a: Platelet-specific proteins (e.g., vWF, Fibrinogen, Platelet Factor 4, PDGF).

cards.q: Structural morphology of platelets on a peripheral blood smear in Gray Platelet Syndrome?
cards.a: Large, pale/gray platelets lacking normal purple azurophilic granulation.

cards.q: Specific substances stored inside platelet dense ($\delta$) granules that are deficient in Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome?
cards.a: ADP, ATP, Serotonin, and Calcium.

cards.q: Oculocutaneous albinism combined with a bleeding diathesis due to dense granule deficiency defines which syndrome?
cards.a: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome.

cards.q: Quantitative functional test used to assess the initial stage of platelet adhesion in clinical practice?
cards.a: Platelet Function Analysis (PFA-100) closure time. High-Yield Lymphoma Mimics and Subtypes

cards.q: Benign, self-limiting lymphadenopathy characterized by follicular hyperplasia and sheets of pale histiocytes with tingible body macrophages?
cards.a: Reactive follicular hyperplasia.

cards.q: Lymphoma variant that characteristically presents as an isolated, enlarging mass in the testis of an elderly man?
cards.a: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL).

cards.q: Distinctive immunohistochemical marker used to identify Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma cells on biopsy?
cards.a: CD20 positive (as they are almost universally diffuse large B-cell lymphomas).

cards.q: Rare B-cell variant that arises within the walls of a chronic fluid-filled cavity, universally driven by HHV-8?
cards.a: Primary Effusion Lymphoma.

cards.q: Slowly progressive T-cell lymphoma presenting with erythroderma, generalized lymphadenopathy, and circulating atypical T-cells with cerebriform nuclei?
cards.a: Sézary Syndrome. Advanced Hemoglobinopathies and Hydrops Fetalis

cards.q: Quantitative percentage of Hemoglobin A ($HbA$) expected on a hemoglobin electrophoresis of a patient with Beta-Thalassemia Major?
cards.a: $0\%$ (completely absent in $\beta^0/\beta^0$ genotypes).

cards.q: Predominant hemoglobin type visualized on electrophoresis in a child with Beta-Thalassemia Major?
cards.a: Hemoglobin F ($\alpha_2\gamma_2$).

cards.q: Quantitative hemoglobin profile diagnostic for Alpha-Thalassemia Minor (trait) in an adult?
cards.a: Normal hemoglobin electrophoresis profile (diagnosed via genetic testing, as no abnormal bands are formed in adults).

cards.q: Specific name given to the dangerous condition where all four alpha-globin genes are deleted?
cards.a: Hydrops fetalis (or Alpha-Thalassemia Major).

cards.q: Cause of tissue hypoxia in a fetus with Hemoglobin Barts ($\gamma_4$)?
cards.a: Hemoglobin Barts has an extremely high oxygen affinity, refusing to release oxygen to peripheral fetal tissues. Oncological Emergencies and Intracellular Lysis

cards.q: Electrocardiogram (ECG) changes expected during acute Tumor Lysis Syndrome due to severe hyperkalemia?
cards.a: Peaked T waves, PR interval prolongation, and widening of the QRS complex.

cards.q: Intravenous medication given in Tumor Lysis Syndrome to stabilize the cardiac myocyte membrane against hyperkalemia?
cards.a: Calcium gluconate (or calcium chloride).

cards.q: Mechanism of action of Rasburicase in managing hyperuricemia?
cards.a: Catalyzes the oxidation of uric acid into allantoin, which is highly soluble and easily excreted by the kidneys.

cards.q: Specific absolute neutrophil count (ANC) calculation formula?
cards.a: $\text{ANC} = \text{WBC} \times (\% \text{Neutrophils} + \% \text{Bands}) / 100$.

cards.q: Most common bacterial pathogens isolated from the blood of patients presenting with febrile neutropenia?
cards.a: Gram-positive cocci (e.g., Staphylococcus epidermidis, Staphylococcus aureus) and Gram-negative bacilli (e.g., Pseudomonas aeruginosa). Direct Oral Anticoagulants (DOACs) and Specific Reversal Agents

cards.q: Most common physiological cause of "Heparin Resistance," where exceptionally high doses of heparin fail to prolong the aPTT?
cards.a: Antithrombin (ATIII) deficiency (inherited or acquired via consumption).

cards.q: Alternative laboratory assay used to accurately monitor Unfractionated Heparin therapy when a patient has a baseline prolonged aPTT?
cards.a: Chromogenic anti-Factor Xa assay.

cards.q: Effect of therapeutic doses of direct oral Factor Xa inhibitors on standard Prothrombin Time (PT) assays?
cards.a: They prolong the PT in a variable, reagent-dependent manner that is unreliable for quantification.

cards.q: Coagulation test that remains completely unaffected by the presence of therapeutic direct oral Factor Xa inhibitors?
cards.a: Thrombin Time (TT) (which only evaluates thrombin-to-fibrin conversion). Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH) & Complement Therapeutics

cards.q: Principal cause of chronic iron deficiency in patients with untreated Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria?
cards.a: Continuous intravascular hemolysis leading to marked, persistent hemosiderinuria and urinary iron loss.

cards.q: Serious infectious complication for which patients must be vaccinated prior to initiating Eculizumab or Ravulizumab therapy?
cards.a: Neisseria meningitidis infection (due to therapeutic blockade of the terminal complement pathway/MAC assembly).

cards.q: Primary mechanism of breakthrough extravascular hemolysis that can occur in PNH patients treated with C5 inhibitors?
cards.a: C3b fragments continue to accumulate on the RBC surface upstream of C5, leading to splenic macrophage clearing.

cards.q: Target of Pegcetacoplan, a newer complement inhibitor used to prevent both intravascular and extravascular hemolysis in PNH?
cards.a: Complement component C3 (and C3b). Myelodysplastic/Myeloproliferative Overlap & Histiocytic Subtleties

cards.q: Minimum percentage of peripheral blood monocytes required over a 3-month period to satisfy WHO diagnostic criteria for CMML?
cards.a: Persistent monocytosis $\ge 10\%$ of the total white blood cell count (and $\ge 1,000/\mu\text{L}$).

cards.q: Distinguishing bone marrow feature that separates Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia (CMML) from Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML)?
cards.a: CMML lacks the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene and shows dominant monocytic proliferation rather than granulocytic.

cards.q: Key diagnostic criteria that separates Juvenile Myelomonocytic Leukemia (JMML) from adult CMML forms?
cards.a: JMML is a childhood disorder strongly linked to mutations in the RAS pathway (e.g., PTPN11, NF1, KRAS) and exhibits elevated Hemoglobin F.

cards.q: Classic radiological description of the bone lesions seen in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis (LCH) of the skull?
cards.a: "Punched-out" lytic lesions without a reactive sclerotic rim.

cards.q: Therapeutic backbone for a patient presenting with severe, life-threatening Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH)?
cards.a: The HLH-94 protocol consisting of Etoposide, Dexamethasone, and Cyclosporine A. Quantitative Platelet Aggregometry Profiles

cards.q: Platelet aggregometry response to ADP, Epinephrine, and Collagen in a patient with Glanzmann Thrombasthenia?
cards.a: Severely impaired or completely absent aggregation.

cards.q: Platelet aggregometry response to Ristocetin in a patient with Glanzmann Thrombasthenia?
cards.a: Normal agglutination (because the GP Ib-IX-V complex is entirely intact).

cards.q: Platelet aggregometry response to ADP, Epinephrine, and Collagen in a patient with Bernard-Soulier Syndrome?
cards.a: Normal aggregation.

cards.q: Platelet aggregometry response to Ristocetin in a patient with Bernard-Soulier Syndrome?
cards.a: Absent agglutination, which does not correct when mixed with normal plasma. Rare T-Cell & Aggressive B-Cell Lymphoma Variants

cards.q: Highly aggressive T-cell lymphoma arising in the background of long-standing, poorly controlled Celiac Disease?
cards.a: Enteropathy-Associated T-Cell Lymphoma (EATL).

cards.q: Primary anatomical location where Enteropathy-Associated T-Cell Lymphoma (EATL) characteristically causes ulceration and perforation?
cards.a: The proximal small intestine (jejunum and ileum).

cards.q: Rare B-cell malignancy that characteristically arises within the walls of a chronic fluid-filled cavity, universally driven by HHV-8?
cards.a: Primary Effusion Lymphoma (PEL).

cards.q: Aggressive Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma presenting as a rapidly expanding, destructive midline mass in the nasal cavity, strongly linked to EBV?
cards.a: Extranodal NK/T-cell Lymphoma, nasal type.

cards.q: Cytogenetic configuration that defines a "Double-Hit" High-Grade B-cell Lymphoma?
cards.a: Concurrent rearrangements of the MYC gene along with either the BCL2 or BCL6 gene. Targeted Oncological Mechanisms & Toxicities

cards.q: Most common long-term, life-threatening organ toxicity associated with the use of Anthracyclines (e.g., Doxorubicin)?
cards.a: Dilated cardiomyopathy (congestive heart failure) due to cumulative, iron-dependent free radical generation.

cards.q: Cardioprotective chelating agent administered alongside Doxorubicin to reduce the risk of anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy?
cards.a: Dexrazoxane.

cards.q: Classic chemotherapeutic agent historically associated with the development of secondary Acute Myeloid Leukemia (sAML) with a short latency period?
cards.a: Etoposide (a Topoisomerase II inhibitor, often associated with $\text{t}(11;23)$ or MLL gene rearrangements).

cards.q: Class-specific adverse effect of Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors like Imatinib related to fluid balance?
cards.a: Fluid retention presenting as periorbital edema, pleural effusions, or peripheral edema.

cards.q: Distinctive pulmonary toxic side effect characteristically associated with Bleomycin therapy?
cards.a: Pulmonary fibrosis (interstitial lung disease), which requires serial pulmonary function testing (DLCO monitoring). Targeted Therapeutics & Precision Mechanisms

cards.q: Specific molecular target of Rituximab used in B-cell lymphomas and autoimmune cytopenias?
cards.a: CD20 surface antigen expressed on mature B cells.

cards.q: Humanized monoclonal antibody targeting CD38 used as a core therapy for relapsed or refractory Multiple Myeloma?
cards.a: Daratumumab.

cards.q: Reversible proteasome inhibitor that disrupts protein homeostasis to induce apoptosis in Multiple Myeloma plasma cells?
cards.a: Bortezomib.

cards.q: Mechanism of action of Brentuximab Vedotin used in Hodgkin Lymphoma?
cards.a: Antibody-drug conjugate targeting CD30 that delivers a microtubule-disrupting agent (MMAE) directly to Reed-Sternberg cells.

cards.q: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapies primarily target which antigen in refractory B-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia?
cards.a: CD19.

cards.q: Unique mechanism of action of Romiplostim used in chronic Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP)?
cards.a: Thrombopoietin (TPO) receptor agonist that stimulates platelet production in the bone marrow. Microenvironment, Iron Transport, and Secondary Anemias

cards.q: Major iron-transport protein responsible for moving iron from enterocytes and macrophages into circulation?
cards.a: Ferroportin.

cards.q: Plasma transport protein that binds toxic free hemoglobin in the blood to prevent oxidative tissue damage?
cards.a: Haptoglobin.

cards.q: Intracellular storage protein that serves as the primary accessible reserve for iron inside hepatocytes and macrophages?
cards.a: Ferritin.

cards.q: Specific physiological site of erythropoietin (EPO) production in the adult human body?
cards.a: Peritubular interstitial cells of the renal cortex.

cards.q: Primary mechanism behind the development of Anemia of Prematurity?
cards.a: Impaired erythropoietin production in response to hypoxia combined with a shortened red blood cell lifespan.

cards.q: Distinctive bone marrow feature that distinguishes Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemia (CDA) from other causes of ineffective erythropoiesis?
cards.a: Marked erythroblast multinuclearity and nuclear bridging. Hypercoagulability Nuances & Endothelial Interactions

cards.q: Autosomal dominant condition causing a mutation in the thrombomodulin gene results in what clinical phenotype?
cards.a: Increased risk of early-onset venous thromboembolism due to impaired activation of Protein C.

cards.q: Impact of severe Hepatic Cirrhosis on a patient's natural anticoagulant systems?
cards.a: Marked reduction in the synthesis of Protein C, Protein S, and Antithrombin, which can paradoxically balance out the loss of procoagulants.

cards.q: Most accurate timing to check for a suspected hereditary Protein S deficiency after an acute deep vein thrombosis?
cards.a: At least 2 weeks after completing acute anticoagulation therapy, as acute thrombosis consumes Protein S.

cards.q: Mechanism by which active malignancies promote a systemic hypercoagulable state (Trousseau syndrome)?
cards.a: Tumor cells secrete tissue factor-bearing microvesicles and mucins that directly activate Factor X.

cards.q: Cardinal clinical presentation that defines May-Thurner Syndrome?
cards.a: Left-sided deep vein thrombosis caused by compression of the left common iliac vein by the overlying right common iliac artery. Histiocytic Profiles & Bone Marrow Borderlands

cards.q: Clonal driver mutation present in approximately 50% of cases of Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis (LCH)?
cards.a: BRAF V600E mutation.

cards.q: Classic immunohistochemical marker that identifies Langerhans cells by staining for the component of Birbeck granules?
cards.a: Langerin (CD207).

cards.q: Standard first-line systemic therapy for multi-system Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis?
cards.a: Vinblastine combined with Prednisone.

cards.q: Life-threatening diagnostic criteria for Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) includes what level of fasting serum triglycerides?
cards.a: Fasting triglycerides $\ge 265\text{ mg/dL}$ (or $\ge 3\text{ mmol/L}$).

cards.q: Diagnostic bone marrow hallmark observed on a core biopsy of a patient with advanced Primary Myelofibrosis?
cards.a: Dense reticulin or collagen fibrosis with a complete absence of normal fat spaces. Rare Coagulopathies & Mixing Study Logistics

cards.q: Coagulation profile (PT, aPTT, bleeding time) characteristically observed in an isolated Factor VII deficiency?
cards.a: Prolonged PT, normal aPTT, and normal bleeding time.

cards.q: Coagulation factor deficiency that characteristically causes a severely prolonged aPTT in vitro but presents with absolutely no clinical bleeding tendency?
cards.a: Factor XII (Hageman factor) deficiency.

cards.q: Diagnostic implication if a patient's prolonged aPTT fails to correct back to normal limits immediately upon a 1:1 mixing study?
cards.a: Indicates the presence of a coagulation inhibitor (e.g., Lupus Anticoagulant or a specific factor antibody).

cards.q: Diagnostic implication if a patient's prolonged aPTT corrects immediately upon a 1:1 mixing study, but prolongs again after a 2-hour incubation?
cards.a: Indicates the presence of a time-dependent, temperature-dependent factor inhibitor (classic for Factor VIII inhibitors).

cards.q: Rare bleeding disorder characterized by a normal PT, normal aPTT, and normal platelet count, but presents with delayed severe hemorrhage after trauma?
cards.a: Factor XIII deficiency.

cards.q: Definitive qualitative screening test used to detect a suspected clinical Factor XIII deficiency?
cards.a: Urea clot solubility test (Factor XIII-deficient clots dissolve rapidly in a 5-molar urea solution). Transfusion Immunology & Metabolic Complications

cards.q: Mechanism behind a Delayed Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction?
cards.a: Anamnestic antibody response against minor red blood cell antigens (such as Kidd or Kell) previously encountered via transfusion or pregnancy.

cards.q: Metabolic complication resulting from the rapid transfusion of multiple units of packed red blood cells stored for an extended period?
cards.a: Hyperkalemia (caused by the gradual leakage of potassium out of aging erythrocytes into the supernatant fluid of the storage bag).

cards.q: Primary mechanism behind Post-Transfusion Purpura (PTP)?
cards.a: Production of alloantibodies against human platelet antigen-1a (HPA-1a) that paradoxically destroy both the transfused and autologous platelets.

cards.q: Processing modification required for blood products given to a patient with a history of severe, IgA-mediated anaphylactic transfusion reactions?
cards.a: Extensive washing of cellular blood products with saline to remove all traces of donor plasma proteins.

cards.q: Direct physiological trigger for Transfusion-Associated Circulatory Overload (TACO)?
cards.a: Rapid infusion of a large volume of blood product exceeding the cardiovascular system's regulatory capacity, increasing hydrostatic pressure. Myeloma Mimics, Heavy Chain Diseases, and Organ Toxicity

cards.q: Distinctive clinical triad that differentiates Waldenström Macroglobulinemia from Multiple Myeloma?
cards.a: Presence of a monoclonal IgM spike, lymphoplasmacytic bone marrow infiltration, and absence of lytic bone lesions.

cards.q: Primary pathophysiological mechanism driving the hyperviscosity syndrome in Waldenström Macroglobulinemia?
cards.a: Large IgM pentamers circulate in high concentrations, significantly increasing plasma resistance and shearing forces.

cards.q: Rare plasma cell dyscrasia characterized by the isolated production of truncated immunoglobulin heavy chains without light chains?
cards.a: Heavy Chain Disease (such as Franklin disease or Seligmann disease).

cards.q: Distinctive organ biopsy finding when examining systemic amyloid deposits under polarized light microscopy?
cards.a: Apple-green birefringence under Congo red staining.

cards.q: Rare systemic disorder presenting with Polyneuropathy, Organomegaly, Endocrinology abnormalities, Monoclonal plasma cell proliferative disorder, and Skin changes?
cards.a: POEMS syndrome.

cards.q: Class-specific, long-term, life-threatening organ toxicity associated with the cumulative use of Anthracyclines like Doxorubicin?
cards.a: Dilated cardiomyopathy due to iron-dependent free radical generation.

cards.q: Cardioprotective chelating agent administered alongside Doxorubicin to mitigate the risk of anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy?
cards.a: Dexrazoxane.

cards.q: Distinctive pulmonary toxic side effect characteristically associated with Bleomycin therapy requiring serial DLCO monitoring?
cards.a: Pulmonary fibrosis. Bone Marrow Microenvironment and Non-Malignant Pancytopenias

cards.q: Key stromal-derived cytokine essential for the survival, homing, and differentiation of early hematopoietic stem cells?
cards.a: Stem Cell Factor (SCF).

cards.q: Specialized microenvironmental structures in the bone marrow where erythroblast maturation and iron transfer occur around a central macrophage?
cards.a: Erythroblastic islands.

cards.q: Autosomal dominant pure red cell aplasia linked to ribosomal protein gene mutations ($RPS19$) presenting in infancy?
cards.a: Diamond-Blackfan Anemia.

cards.q: Distinctive physical exam sign on the hands that differentiates Diamond-Blackfan Anemia from Fanconi Anemia?
cards.a: Triphalangeal thumbs in Diamond-Blackfan; absent or hypoplastic thumbs and radii in Fanconi.

cards.q: Acquired pure red cell aplasia (PRCA) in adults is classically associated with what encapsulated anterior mediastinal tumor?
cards.a: Thymoma.

cards.q: Rare, inherited normocytic anemia characterized by multinucleated erythroblasts, nuclear bridging, and a positive acidified serum lysis (Ham) test?
cards.a: Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemia (CDA). Hemoglobinopathies: Structural Variants and Technical Testing

cards.q: Structural hemoglobin variant that defines Hemoglobin C disease?
cards.a: Lysine substitution for glutamic acid at position 6 of the beta-globin chain.

cards.q: Classic morphology of erythrocytes on a peripheral blood smear from a patient with homozygous Hemoglobin CC disease?
cards.a: Hexagonal, rod-shaped intracellular HbC crystals and target cells.

cards.q: Structural variant where glutamic acid is replaced by lysine at position 26 of the beta-globin chain, highly prevalent in Southeast Asia?
cards.a: Hemoglobin E ($HbE$).

cards.q: Underlying genetic mechanism responsible for the vast majority of Alpha-Thalassemia cases?
cards.a: Large structural gene deletions via unequal chromosomal crossing over.

cards.q: Underlying genetic mechanism responsible for the vast majority of Beta-Thalassemia cases?
cards.a: Point mutations affecting globin mRNA splicing, promoter regions, or translation termination.

cards.q: Normal minor adult hemoglobin variant formed by two alpha chains and two delta chains ($\alpha_2\delta_2$)?
cards.a: Hemoglobin $A_2$ ($HbA_2$).

cards.q: Definitive quantitative assay used to precisely measure and monitor Hemoglobin S levels in sickle cell patients undergoing exchange transfusion?
cards.a: High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC). Immune and Non-Immune Hemolytic Footprints

cards.q: Humanized monoclonal antibody targeting complement component C5 used to treat Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria and atypical HUS?
cards.a: Eculizumab.

cards.q: Physical footprint of intravascular hemolysis measured via a marked decrease in which specific serum transport protein?
cards.a: Haptoglobin.

cards.q: Oxidation product of hemoglobin breakdown that accumulates in the renal tubules and urine during sustained, severe intravascular hemolysis?
cards.a: Hemosiderin (Hemosiderinuria).

cards.q: Protozoal intraerythrocytic infection that mimics G6PD deficiency by inducing hemolytic anemia and forming "Maltese cross" tetrads on a thick smear?
cards.a: Babesiosis.

cards.q: Metabolic pathway in which Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase (G6PD) operates to protect RBCs from oxidative stress?
cards.a: Hexose monophosphate (HMP) shunt.

cards.q: Diagnostic pitfall when testing G6PD enzyme activity levels immediately after an acute hemolytic crisis?
cards.a: False-negative result due to the destruction of older, enzyme-deficient RBCs and a high concentration of young, enzyme-replete reticulocytes. Secondary Myeloproliferative States and Reactive Changes

cards.q: Principal bone marrow cytokine responsible for driving the extensive reactive collagen fibrosis in Primary Myelofibrosis?
cards.a: Transforming Growth Factor-beta (TGF-$\beta$) released from clonal megakaryocytes.

cards.q: Name given to the dry tap bone marrow aspiration attempt classic in both Primary Myelofibrosis and Hairy Cell Leukemia?
cards.a: Punctio sicca.

cards.q: Most common physiological cause of a secondary polycythemia presenting with elevated erythropoietin (EPO) levels?
cards.a: Chronic hypoxemia due to severe lung disease, sleep apnea, high altitude, or right-to-left shunts.

cards.q: Paraneoplastic condition where a renal cell carcinoma or cerebellar hemangioblastoma causes erythrocytosis?
cards.a: Inappropriate secondary polycythemia via autonomous EPO production.

cards.q: Pathophysiological driver of erythromelalgia presenting as burning pain and erythema in the extremities of patients with Essential Thrombocythemia?
cards.a: Platelet microvascular occlusion and subsequent localized endothelial inflammation.

cards.q: Expected Leukocyte Alkaline Phosphatase (LAP) score trend in Chronic Myeloid Leukemia versus a benign Leukemoid Reaction?

topic: Infectious Disease — Sepsis, HIV, fungal & parasitic infections

cards.q: First-line empiric treatment for native valve infective endocarditis?
cards.a: Vancomycin plus Ceftriaxone.

cards.q: Most common causative organism of acute infective endocarditis in IV drug users?
cards.a: Staphylococcus aureus.

cards.q: Classic valvular pathology seen in intravenous drug users with endocarditis?
cards.a: Tricuspid regurgitation.

cards.q: Mechanism of action of Vancomycin?
cards.a: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to the D-Ala-D-Ala terminus of peptidoglycan precursors.

cards.q: Mechanism of action of Daptomycin?
cards.a: Disrupts cell membrane function by creating transmembrane channels causing intracellular ion leakage.

cards.q: Major adverse effect of Daptomycin that requires weekly monitoring?
cards.a: Myopathy and elevated Creatine Kinase (CK) levels.

cards.q: Why is Daptomycin ineffective in treating bacterial pneumonia?
cards.a: It is inactivated by pulmonary surfactant.

cards.q: Empiric treatment for a patient with suspected bacterial meningitis aged 2 to 50 years?
cards.a: Vancomycin plus a third-generation cephalosporin (Ceftriaxone or Cefotaxime).

cards.q: Crucial antibiotic addition to empiric meningitis treatment for patients over 50 or immunocompromised?
cards.a: Ampicillin.

cards.q: Why is Ampicillin added to empiric meningitis regimens in older or vulnerable adults?
cards.a: To cover Listeria monocytogenes.

cards.q: Which adjunctive medication should be given prior to or with the first dose of antibiotics in pneumococcal meningitis?
cards.a: Dexamethasone.

cards.q: Most common cause of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) across all age groups?
cards.a: Streptococcus pneumoniae.

cards.q: Empirical outpatient treatment for a healthy adult with Community-Acquired Pneumonia and no comorbidities?
cards.a: Amoxicillin, Doxycycline, or a Macrolide (if local resistance is <25%).

cards.q: Empirical inpatient (non-ICU) treatment for Community-Acquired Pneumonia?
cards.a: A respiratory fluoroquinolone (e.g., Levofloxacin) OR a beta-lactam plus a macrolide.

cards.q: Drug of choice for treating severe Clostridioides difficile infection?
cards.a: Oral Vancomycin or Fidaxomicin. HIV, Opportunistic Infections, and Prophylaxis

cards.q: CD4 count threshold below which prophylaxis for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) is indicated?
cards.a: <200 cells/mm³.

cards.q: First-line agent used for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) prophylaxis?
cards.a: Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX).

cards.q: CD4 count threshold below which prophylaxis for Toxoplasma gondii is indicated in seropositive patients?
cards.a: <100 cells/mm³.

cards.q: Medication used for Toxoplasma gondii prophylaxis?
cards.a: Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX).

cards.q: Diagnostic finding on a brain MRI for an HIV patient with Toxoplasma gondii encephalitis?
cards.a: Multiple ring-enhancing lesions with a preference for the basal ganglia.

cards.q: Preferred treatment for active Toxoplasma encephalitis?
cards.a: Pyrimethamine plus Sulfadiazine (plus Leucovorin).

cards.q: Opportunistic infection causing painful, linear esophageal ulcers in an HIV patient?
cards.a: Cytomegalovirus (CMV).

cards.q: Opportunistic infection causing round, punched-out esophageal ulcers in an HIV patient?
cards.a: Herpes Simplex Virus 1 (HSV-1).

cards.q: Diagnostic finding on a fundoscopic exam for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis?
cards.a: Pizzalike retinopathy showing perivascular hemorrhages and fluffy white exudates.

cards.q: First-line treatment for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis?
cards.a: Ganciclovir or Valganciclovir.

cards.q: CD4 count threshold below which primary prophylaxis for Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) was historically indicated (no longer routinely required if ART is started immediately)?
cards.a: <50 cells/mm³.

cards.q: Preferred treatment for an active Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) infection?
cards.a: Azithromycin or Clarithromycin combined with Ethambutol.

cards.q: Most common central nervous system fungal infection in HIV patients?
cards.a: Cryptococcal meningitis.

cards.q: Initial diagnostic test visualizing encapsulated yeasts in cerebrospinal fluid via negative staining?
cards.a: India ink preparation.

cards.q: Most sensitive and specific rapid diagnostic test for Cryptococcal meningitis?
cards.a: Cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) lateral flow assay.

cards.q: Induction therapy regimen for Cryptococcal meningitis?
cards.a: Liposomal Amphotericin B plus Flucytosine.

cards.q: Maintenance therapy agent for Cryptococcal meningitis after induction?
cards.a: Fluconazole.

cards.q: Form of skin lesion associated with Human Herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) in HIV patients?
cards.a: Kaposi sarcoma. Tick-Borne and Zoonotic Diseases

cards.q: Causative organism of Lyme disease?
cards.a: Borrelia burgdorferi.

cards.q: Classic initial dermatological presentation of Lyme disease?
cards.a: Erythema migrans (bull's-eye rash).

cards.q: Vector responsible for transmitting Lyme disease and Anaplasmosis?
cards.a: Ixodes tick.

cards.q: First-line oral antibiotic for early localized Lyme disease in adults?
cards.a: Doxycycline.

cards.q: Preferred antibiotic for Lyme disease in pregnant patients or children under 8?
cards.a: Amoxicillin.

cards.q: Manifestation of late disseminated Lyme disease involving the joints?
cards.a: Asymmetric monoarticular or oligoarticular arthritis, usually affecting the knee.

cards.q: Causative organism of Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever (RMSF)?
cards.a: Rickettsia rickettsii.

cards.q: Classic progression of the rash in Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever?
cards.a: Starts on the wrists and ankles and spreads centripetally to the trunk, palms, and soles.

cards.q: Drug of choice for Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever in ALL patients, including children and pregnant women?
cards.a: Doxycycline.

cards.q: Tick-borne disease characterized by hemolytic anemia, jaundice, and a Maltese cross appearance on blood smear?
cards.a: Babesiosis.

cards.q: Vector for Babesia microti?
cards.a: Ixodes tick.

cards.q: First-line antimicrobial combination for mild-to-moderate Babesiosis?
cards.a: Atovaquone plus Azithromycin.

cards.q: Tick-borne illness characterized by leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, elevated liver enzymes, and morulae inside monocytes?
cards.a: Human Monocytic Ehrlichiosis (HME). Tuberculosis & Mycobacterial Diseases

cards.q: Standard 4-drug regimen for initial treatment of active Tuberculosis (TB)?
cards.a: Rifampin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide, and Ethambutol (RIPE).

cards.q: Mechanism of action of Isoniazid?
cards.a: Inhibits the synthesis of mycolic acids, an essential component of the mycobacterial cell wall.

cards.q: Common adverse effect of Isoniazid preventable by co-administering Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine)?
cards.a: Peripheral neuropathy.

cards.q: Mechanism of action of Rifampin?
